Title: Malaysia's online job vacancies surge 17.8pct to 654,655 in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's online job offerings has risen 17.8 per cent to 654,655 in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, with advertising and marketing professionals recording the highest demand among occupations.
The Statistics Department said 95,102 companies advertised job vacancies during the quarter, up from 79,510 in the second quarter of 2026.
Professionals accounted for the largest share of online job offerings, at 47.1 per cent or 308,137 vacancies, compared with 285,907 in the preceding quarter.
Technicians and associate professionals recorded 110,180 job offerings, followed by managers with 96,442.
Among individual occupations, advertising and marketing professionals topped the list with 44,989 job offerings.
This was followed by administrative associate professionals (29,708), managing directors and chief executives (27,915), accountants and auditors (23,562), and software developers (18,109).
By economic sector, services continued to account for the largest share of online job offerings, at 49.7 per cent or 325,520 vacancies, compared with 43.9 per cent in the second quarter.
Within the sector, wholesale and retail trade, repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles recorded the highest number of job offerings at 90,613.
This was followed by professional, scientific and technical activities (50,220), other service activities (37,518), administrative and support service activities (35,263), and manufacturing (30,495).
In the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) field, technicians recorded the highest number of job offerings at 8,306, followed by sales managers (5,001) and marketing executives (4,810).
The same occupation also topped demand in the science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) field, with 8,306 job offerings, followed by engineers (4,343) and quantity surveyors (4,294).
Under the critical occupations List (COL), sales executives recorded the highest demand with 9,772 job offerings, followed by assistant managers (9,520) and account executives (9,290).
The department said its Big Data Analytics: Job Market Insights Online Job Offerings Advertised in Malaysia (Q3 2026) report provides job seekers with insights into demand across occupations, economic sectors, TVET, STEM and COL.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan Palace: Ismail's resignation as MB yet to be verified
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Palace has taken note of the statement by Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir regarding Datuk Ismail Lasim's resignation menteri besar.
However, the Secretary of the Royal Household, in a statement today, said the Palace had yet to verify the authenticity of the letter, which Zambry said had been signed by Ismail.
"Under the State Constitution, any resignation by the menteri besar must be submitted to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, and will only take effect upon receiving his consent.
"However, it must be emphasised that the Palace has yet to verify the authenticity of the resignation letter," said the statement.
The secretary said the resignation letter was delivered to Istana Hinggap in Seremban at 12.16am on Nov 17.
The letter, he added, was handed over by a man who identified himself as Hamidi from the law firm Shahrul Hamidi & Haziq.
"(Tuanku Muhriz's) private secretary had conveyed to Datuk Ismail Lasim via WhatsApp, at 8.38pm, that His Royal Highness consented to give him an audience, as requested, and this was acknowledged by him.
"The audience with Tuanku Muhriz has been scheduled for 10am on Friday.
"His Royal Highness's consent for the audience was granted 80 minutes before Zambry's announcement on his Facebook account informing the public of Ismail's resignation," he said.
Yesterday, Zambry had said Ismail had submitted a
resignation letter
to Tuanku Muhriz.
He said Barisan Nasional chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had also received a copy of the resignation letter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wangsa Maju LRT crowding sparks passenger complaints
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Crowding at Wangsa Maju LRT station today led to the closure of an escalator, with commuters claiming they had to wait up to 15 minutes to access the platform.
The congestion prompted complaints on social media, with commuters questioning why no advance notification had been issued through the operator's app.
In a post on Threads, one commuter said there had been no warning despite the growing crowds.
"Wangsa Maju LRT is so packed that they had to close the escalator. The app isn't working! At least send some kind of notification. It's been packed for 15 minutes," the commuter wrote.
The commuter later said an empty train had been sent to Setiawangsa LRT station to pick up passengers and that they had managed to continue their journey to Kampung Baru.
Other users also shared their experiences, with some saying they had been forced to queue on the stairs. Others praised commuters for maintaining orderly queues despite the disruption.
Rapid KL, in a response on its Threads account @myrapidkl, apologised for the inconvenience and said an empty train had been sent to the station.
It said operations staff would manage passenger movement to prevent overcrowding on the platform, including closing escalators when passenger numbers surged.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Marcos wants Asean, East Asia to turn commitments into food, energy security
Article:
MANILA: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Tuesday urged Southeast Asian and East Asian leaders to translate regional cooperation into concrete safeguards for food and energy supplies, stressing that global disruptions must not leave households facing higher costs and businesses struggling to operate, The Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported.
In opening the 29th Asean Plus Three (APT) Summit, Marcos said the impact of conflicts, supply disruptions and other shocks thousands of miles away can quickly reach East and Southeast Asia through rising rice prices, energy costs and lost income.
"A disruption thousands of miles away can reach households across East and Southeast Asia through the price of rice, the cost of energy, or the loss of a day's income," he said.
The Asean Plus Three framework brings together the 11 Asean member states and China, Japan and South Korea.
Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Chinese Minister on Agriculture and Rural Affairs Zhang Zhu joined the talks along with other Asean leaders.
Marcos said the region must ensure that cooperation produces tangible results, particularly in keeping maritime trade and logistics moving and securing essential supplies.
"Our task today is to put our collective strength to work. In ships reaching their destinations, in reliable supplies of food and energy, in businesses continuing to operate, and in families facing the future with greater confidence," he said.
He cited the Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralisation (CMIM) and the Asean Plus Three Emergency Rice Reserve (APTERR) as existing mechanisms that provide a foundation for regional economic stability and cooperation during emergencies.
The CMIM is a multilateral currency swap arrangement designed to safeguard the APT region against short-term liquidity and balance-of-payments difficulties while the APTERR is a permanent regional cooperation mechanism established in 2011 to strengthen food security, poverty alleviation, and malnourishment eradication, and to stabilise rice price volatility caused by climate change or natural disasters without distorting trade.
Marcos said these arrangements would be increasingly important as conflict, supply disruptions, financial uncertainty and natural disasters put additional pressure on regional economies.
Marcos said the partnership remains an important platform for stability, resilience and shared prosperity amid growing global fragmentation.
As the cooperation framework approaches its 30th anniversary, he urged leaders to make the benefits of their agreements more directly felt by their people.
"Let us renew our ambition for this partnership and shorten the distance between the commitments we make around this table and the benefits our peoples feel in their daily lives," he said.
The regional leaders meet as the ongoing conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran in the Middle East triggered severe global fuel and energy crisis, driven by disruptions and security pressures around key transit corridors like the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most vital energy chokepoint.
The strait carries roughly 20 per cent to 25 per cent of global petroleum and oil supplies and about 20 per cent of global liquefied natural gas exports.

Title: 11 men arrested after Sandakan market clash
Article:
SANDAKAN: Police have arrested 11 men in connection with a clash between two groups at Pasar Bandar Ramai-Ramai in Sandakan last night.
The suspects, aged between 15 and 46, included six Filipinos.
A video of the fight has also circulated on social media.
Sandakan police chief Assistant Commissioner George Abd Rakman said police received information through the emergency hotline about the clash, which was believed to have involved sharp weapons.
"The incident is believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between two groups," he said in a statement.

Title: RTD: Many VIPs, influencers driving luxury vehicles without insurance, road tax
Article:
ALOR STAR: VIPs and social media influencers were among those detained by the Kedah Road Transport Department for driving luxury vehicles without valid road tax and insurance coverage.
State RTD director Stien Van Lutam said some of them gave excuses such as forgetting to renew their insurance, while others claimed to own too many vehicles.
He said some resorted to such actions due to financial difficulties and being blacklisted, yet continued to flaunt their wealth by driving luxury vehicles daily.
Among the vehicles which were seized by the department, he said, were BYD, Porsche, BMW and Mercedes models as Toyota Vellfires.
"Whatever excuses are given, we will not compromise as this involves road traffic laws.
"There are serious implications with vehicles without insurance coverage in the event of an accident, particularly when it comes to claims," he said when met at the Kedah RTD headquarters.
Stien said the excuses which were given were treated merely as attempts to get the drivers off the hook, so they did not matter.
He said things have changed, as RTD officers are now equipped with modern technology — the Smart Enforcement Device (SmED) — throughout the operation, codenamed Op Luxury.
He added that the device enables RTD officers to quickly detect vehicle-related offences, particularly those involving the absence of valid road tax, insurance coverage and driving licences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Body of man with star-shaped tattoo found floating in river
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The body of a man with a star-shaped tattoo on the right side of his neck was found floating in a river near Kampung Merbau Sempak, Sungai Buloh, on Friday.
Sungai Buloh police chief Superintendent Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said police were alerted to the discovery by the public about 9.35am.
"The identity of the deceased has yet to be established. The body of the heavyset man was found without a shirt, wearing only blue jeans and socks," he said in a statement yesterday.
He said an examination revealed injuries to the deceased's left arm, adding that no identification documents were found on the body.
"A post-mortem examination was conducted about 7.40pm on the same day at the Puncak Alam UiTM Hospital. The case has been classified as sudden death," he said.
Hafiz urged anyone who may have information about the man's identity or whose family member is missing to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohamad Hafiz Seleman at 016-4507492 or the Sungai Buloh police headquarters at 03-61561222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Achi Jaya takes over Boustead Plantations for RM4.3bil?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) has chosen Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd to take over Boustead Plantations Bhd (BPlant) at an estimated price of RM4.3 billion, sources told Berita Harian.
Achi Jaya is understood to have beaten SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd for the takeover, two companies with larger-scale plantation operations.
According to the sources, the decision has been made although details of the acquisition structure, equity interest involved and payment terms have yet to be made public.
The amount also drew attention when compared with Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd's (KLK) proposed acquisition of BPlant in 2023, which valued the plantation company's entire equity at about RM3.47 billion.
On Aug 24, 2023, KLK entered into an agreement to buy a 33 per cent stake in BPlant from Boustead Holdings Bhd at RM1.55 per share, in a transaction valued at RM1.15 billion.
However, the transaction was terminated on Oct 4 that year.
According to its 2025 Integrated Report, SD Guthrie has a total land bank of 703,115 hectares across several countries.
Of this, 557,258 hectares comprise oil palm planted areas, including 292,122 hectares in Malaysia.
Tradewinds Plantation, meanwhile, has a total land bank of 156,138 hectares, witj about 87 per cent being planted with oil palm and rubber.
In comparison, the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification documents for Achi Jaya recorded 11,702 hectares of oil palm planted area within the scope of its audit in November 2025.
However, this figure does not necessarily cover the company's entire operations.
BPlant, meanwhile, reportedly has a land bank of 97,500 hectare, including about 72,200 hectares of oil palm planted area.
Based on the planted area recorded in Achi Jaya's MSPO audit, the company could potentially manage 83,902 hectares of oil palm planted area following its acquisition.
This estimate, however, is based on the assumption that all of BPlant's oil palm planted areas are included in the transaction and that there is no overlap in assets.
If the RM4.3 billion refers to BPlant's entire equity value, the figure would be about RM830 million or 23.9 per cent higher than the RM3.47 billion valuation under KLK's proposed transaction in 2023.
However, a direct comparison can only be made once Achi Jaya's transaction structure is confirmed, including whether the RM4.3 billion price tag covers BPlant's entire equity or only a specific stake.
Achi Jaya Plantations is a privately held company incorporated on Feb 10, 2001, and is involved in oil palm cultivation and milling, as well as hotel management and operations.
According to its November 2025 MSPO audit report, Achi Jaya's operations within the scope of certification comprise Sungei Gerchang Estate, Johore Labis Estate and Claire Estate in Chaah, Johor.
LTAT recently come under the spotlight in Parliament after Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin confirmed the sale of its leasehold interest in a piece of land in Ampang Hilir, Kuala Lumpur, to the US government for RM420 million.
Mohamed Khaled was reported to have said on Oct 26 that the transaction, which was conducted through a tender process, was for the construction of a new US embassy.
He explained that the disposal was part of LTAT's efforts to rebalance its asset portfolio, while ensuring compliance with relevant policies, procedures and governance requirements.
The ownership of the land remains with the Federal Lands Commissioner, as the transaction involved only the leasehold interest.
Under the proposed BPlant acquisition, the transaction value, payment terms and the buyer's ability to manage the plantation assets are among the key considerations in safeguarding the long-term interests of LTAT, members of the Malaysian armed forces and its contributors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: No dedicated digital map of illegal border routes, high-risk areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities have identified 443 illegal routes and 281 hotspots used by smugglers since January.
However, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said enforcement agencies do not yet have a dedicated digital geospatial map of these locations.
"At present, the border security enforcement agencies do not yet have a dedicated digital geospatial data map that records in detail the locations of illegal routes, high-risk areas, control weak points or locations needing immediate security intervention.
"However, security control and monitoring in those areas are carried out continuously through strategic measures by the General Operations Force (GOF)," he told the Dewan Rakyat.
Saifuddin was responding in a written reply to Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar), who asked about the status of digital mapping of the Malaysia-Thailand border in Perlis.
Rushdan also asked about identifying "rat trails", high-risk areas, control weak points and locations needing immediate security intervention, as well as if the government had an integrated geospatial database that could be used in a controlled manner.
Saifuddin said the illegal routes and hotspots included those in Sabah and Sarawak.
To tackle illegal routes, he said, GOF carried out regular border security control through the use of fixed posts along the border line, checks at Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) complexes, foot and vehicle patrols, roadblocks and intelligence gathering.
He said the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry, through the Survey and Mapping Department, was responsible for marking and surveying international boundaries.
The department also maintains the geospatial data related to the boundary, which serves as base data to support mapping, analysis and planning by government agencies, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: United Airlines resolves technology issue that disrupted departing flights
Article:
WASHINGTON: United Airlines said it has resolved a technology-related issue that disrupted some departing flights earlier Monday, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
"Earlier today, we experienced a technology-related issue that impacted some departing flights. The issue has been resolved," it said on the US social media platform X.
The airline did not disclose the cause of the technical issue, the number of flights affected or the total number of passengers impacted.
The latest disruption comes after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday following a communications problem affecting air traffic control facilities.
The FAA's decision temporarily halted flights at airports across the country, with the suspension lasting more than four hours.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy later announced at a news conference that the restrictions had been lifted and US airspace had reopened.
The nationwide disruption resulted in thousands of flight delays and cancellations, affecting travellers and airline operations across the US.
- 'We need brand-new software'
Speaking to Fox News, Duffy said Monday that this was not an FAA system-wide problem.
"I don't know what the root cause of United is," he added.
Duffy stressed that "new software" is needed.
"The software we use to manage our airplanes in the airspace was built in the 1990s. It works. It works well. But if we're going to drive more safety and more efficiency, we need brand-new software," he said.
He implored Congress for additional FAA funding.
"I'm hoping that Congress, on a bipartisan effort, will make the investments that haven't been made for decades ... So if we get the money, I promise that Congress, America, (President) Donald Trump and I will continue to deliver on these historic investments that change the future of aviation in America," he said.
Separately, speaking to Fox News, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said both the homeland and the banking system remain "secure" following recent nationwide infrastructure and telecommunications disruptions. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Costa Rican journalist gunned down near capital
Article:
SAN JOSE: Costa Rican independent journalist Camilo Rodriguez, who had called out alleged ties between drug traffickers and politicians on social media, was shot dead on Monday outside the capital San Jose, authorities said.
Two men riding on a motorcycle opened fire on Rodriguez as he was driving through the town of Santo Domingo de Heredia, police chief Raul Rivera said.
Rodriguez, 50, had reported receiving several death threats from drug trafficking groups.
He would name drug lords by their full names and claimed to have provided reports to the US Drug Enforcement Administration regarding links between drug traffickers and powerful figures in politics and business.
When President Laura Fernandez was running for office last year, she sued Rodriguez for defamation after he posted a video claiming her home had been built with money allegedly provided by a drug trafficker.
"Regardless of the content of his statements, what happened today in our country is a stain on freedom of expression," Fernandez said in a video released by her office.
Rodriguez ran for president in 2022 but his nomination was rejected by electoral authorities on technical grounds.
He also accused his ex-wife of being involved in drug trafficking. She has filed a complaint alleging he sexually abused their children.
The Costa Rican Journalists' Association condemned his killing and demanded "a swift investigation".
"All evidence so far points to the silencing of a dissenting voice in Costa Rica – a person who published information about organised crime in the country," the association's president, Yanancy Noguera, told AFP.
In recent years, Costa Rica has gone from being a drug transit point to a logistics hub for trafficking, and has lost its status as one of the safest countries in Central America.
Fernandez, who took office in May, campaigned on a promise to crack down on the crime wave, and said she is drawing inspiration from El Salvador's iron-fisted President Nayib Bukele.
Attorney General Carlo Diaz announced an investigation into the murder, adding that Rodriguez – who had contributed to various Costa Rican print, radio and television media outlets and more recently turned to social media – had declined to enter a witness protection programme.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flying Doctor Service suspension affects 85 interior Sarawak localities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eighty-five localities covered by the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) in the interiors of Sarawak have been affected after the service was temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash in September.
The Health Ministry said, of that number, 16 localities were identified as having no access via alternative land and water transport.
"The ministry temporarily suspended FDS operations to allow a full investigation and assessment of the service's safety and operational aspects," it said in a written reply posted on Parliament's official website.
It was responding to a question from Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (PN-Merbok), who asked for details on the number of areas affected by the temporary halt of the FDS in interior Sarawak, the alternatives provided, and the maximum period for patients to obtain treatment in emergencies.
To reduce the impact on affected communities, the ministry said several measures have been taken to ensure service continuity through the optimisation of land and water routes and the activation of referral and alternative transport mechanisms.
Priority is given to localities based on clinical risk, degree of remoteness and the availability of alternative access, the ministry said.
For emergency cases during this temporary suspension, the ministry said it ensures every patient receives immediate action based on clinical priority through the emergency medical evacuation (Medevac) service or suitable alternative transport.
To that end, the ministry is working with the Fire and Rescue Department and other agencies to help manage emergency cases and ensure continuity of access to emergency treatment for interior residents, taking into account weather conditions, road conditions, asset availability and operational safety.
On Sept 8, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail Lasim: Sorry, but I don't have anything to say right now
Article:
SEREMBAN: Datuk Ismail Lasim, who resigned as Negri Sembilan menteri besar yesterday, is remaining tightlipped over his and the state's future.
"Sorry... no PC (press conference) or press statetement from me. Thank you for your cooperation and friendship," was all he would say when contacted.
The Juasseh assemblyman asked for some time and space to attend to several administrative matters.
Ismail's resignation was confirmed by Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir yesterday. (https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/1579249/ismail-resigns-negri-sembilan-mb)
He had said Ismail had sent his resignation letter to Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, adding that BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy.
Ismail's resignation after just 106 days in charge of the state government, having been sworn in on Aug 2, has raised questions about the actual reasons behind his move.
This is particularly so as the customary and administrative crisis in Negri Sembilan continues to draw public attention.
Just days earlier, Ismail had said discussions to resolve the crisis were showing positive progress.
He had also expressed his commitment to ensuring that the proposed state legislative assembly sitting on Nov 26, followed by the tabling of the state's 2027 Budget, would proceed as planned.
This was after Ismail and the 10 former state executive council members had withdrawn the letter to the Keeper of the Rulers' Seal regarding Tuanku Muhriz's status as Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
He had said he hoped that the withdrawal of the letter would help solve the constitutional crises in the state.
Sources said Ismail's resignation came as a surprise as he was said to have already gotten a date for an audience with Tuanku Muhriz to seek the ruler's consent for the legislative assembly sitting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MetMalaysia: Thunderstorms, strong winds until 1pm in Perak, Pahang, Sabah
Article:

Title: KLCC oversupply masks growing demand for premium homes, says Paramount
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Despite a softening property market and concerns over oversupply in Kuala Lumpur, Paramount Corp Bhd remains confident in the resilience of the city's high-end residential segment, underpinned by rising regional wealth, stronger foreign buyer interest and growing demand for larger homes in prime urban locations.
While the oversupply situation in Kuala Lumpur, particularly around the KLCC area, has become slightly more pronounced in 2026, Paramount believes the market needs to be viewed through a more differentiated lens.
Not all segments are facing the same challenges, with the bulk of the existing overhang concentrated in different product categories from the premium residential market that the group is targeting, Paramount Group chief executive officer Jeffrey Chew told Business Times.
He said the company takes a highly research-driven approach before embarking on any development, carefully assessing the underlying demand and buyer profile for each project.
"What we are seeing is that, over the last 18 months, interest from foreign buyers in Malaysia has grown quite substantially. At the same time, wealth creation across Southeast Asia and the wider Asian region has been tremendous.
"This has created an increasingly affluent buyer pool, with more people moving up from the middle-market segment into higher-end properties. They are searching for larger homes, better specifications and more prestigious urban addresses.
"While there is an oversupply in certain segments, we believe the demand for well-located, premium residential properties remains strong," he said.
Paramount's confidence is supported by the performance of its Ashwood development, which has demonstrated the depth of demand for larger, high-end residences in Kuala Lumpur.
The project, which is currently under construction, was fully sold within 18 months of its launch in 2024, with units priced between RM1.5 million and RM4.3 million.
Notably, about 70 per cent of its buyers were foreigners, coming from markets including China, Taiwan, Japan, Europe, Australia and New Zealand.
The development attracted buyers seeking larger living spaces, with built-up areas ranging from about 1,500 sq ft to 4,000 sq ft.
Chew said the response to Ashwood reinforced the group's view that there remains a distinct market for premium homes, particularly among affluent international buyers who value location, space and quality.
The project is expected to be completed in 2028.
"We were very encouraged by the response to Ashwood. It demonstrated that there is still a sizeable market for larger, premium residential units, particularly among foreign buyers.
"That gives us confidence as we move forward with The Ashbourne, where we expect to see a similar profile of buyers," he said.
Paramount is now looking to build on that success through The Ashbourne, its RM1.3 billion residential development and its third project in the prestigious U-Thant enclave of Kuala Lumpur.
The development will comprise two towers housing 458 high-end serviced residences, with built-up areas ranging from 1,491 sq ft to 2,661 sq ft. Prices will range from RM1.8 million to slightly above RM4 million per unit, or about RM1,350 per sq ft.
Chew acknowledged that market conditions have become more challenging since the launch of Ashwood in 2024, with the property market showing signs of softening in 2026.
This has prompted the group to take a more cautious view of buyer demand, particularly regarding whether foreign purchasers would maintain their interest and whether domestic buyers could provide sufficient depth to absorb the new supply.
Nevertheless, he believes The Ashbourne is well-positioned to capture demand from the premium market.
"We are conscious that the market has softened somewhat. Naturally, we have to consider whether foreign buyers will continue to come into the market and whether local buyers will be able to absorb the supply.
"But we remain cautiously confident. Construction and material costs have increased significantly over the years, and the trend has also influenced the pricing of new developments.
"We have started our pre-registration exercise, and the initial response has been encouraging. We believe The Ashbourne can attract a fairly positive response," he said.
The project is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2030.
He said beyond the development itself, Paramount's partnership with Japan's Mitsui Fudosan represents a strategic step in strengthening its international profile and expanding its reach among overseas property buyers.
Under the joint venture, Mitsui Fudosan (Asia) Malaysia Sdn Bhd will acquire a 49 per cent equity interest in Meridian Kuasa Sdn Bhd for RM23.1 million, while Paramount retains a controlling 51 per cent stake.
Meridian Kuasa will serve as the development vehicle for The Ashbourne, with Paramount leading project management, sales and marketing.
Chew said Paramount had deliberately sought a strong international partner, recognising that securing a prestigious development site alone would not be enough to establish its presence in the global residential market.
"Mitsui Fudosan is a major international property player with an established presence in malls, commercial assets and high-rise developments.
"We knew that if we wanted to attract a partner of this calibre, we had to secure a very good piece of land with strong development potential.
"One of our objectives when acquiring the land was to take our brand beyond Malaysia. We believe Mitsui Fudosan is the right partner because of its strong international reputation.
"When we market the development overseas, having a recognised international name alongside Paramount will help strengthen buyers' confidence in our product," he said.
The partnership also provides a platform for potential future collaboration, bringing together Mitsui Fudosan's international experience and market reach with Paramount's local development expertise.
Despite its growing focus on premium developments, Chew stressed that Paramount was not abandoning its traditional role as a people's developer.
The group will continue to cater to the needs of Malaysian homebuyers while expanding its portfolio to address the changing aspirations of a more affluent regional buyer base.
He said the strategy was not about moving away from the group's core market but rather responding to the evolution of wealth and purchasing power across Malaysia and the wider region.
"We are still very much the people's developers. Internally, that remains our philosophy. We want to meet the housing needs of people, both in Malaysia and overseas.
"At the same time, we recognise that wealth across Southeast Asia and Asia has grown significantly. Buyers' aspirations have evolved, and there is a growing segment looking for larger homes, premium products and more affluent locations.
"We want to participate in that growth, but we are certainly not abandoning our bread-and-butter business," he said.
Meanwhile, Paramount said in a statement today that it has appointed branding agency IMAJEN to develop the brand strategy and creative positioning for The Ashbourne.
Evon Chong, co-founder of IMAJEN, said the projects that matter most to developers usually carry an ambition to move the brand forward," he said.
"Visionary developers are rarely looking to repeat what has already been done, even when it has been successful," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 89pct of private health facilities display medicine prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 5,332 of the 5,986 private health facilities and community pharmacies monitored have started displaying medicine prices, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad told the Dewan Rakyat.
The figure represents 89.1 per cent of the premises monitored by the Health Ministry between May 2025 and September 2026, he said.
Of the total, 3,905 premises (65.2 per cent) achieved a satisfactory level of price display, while 649 (10.8 per cent) had yet to display medicine prices.
Dzulkefly said this in a written parliamentary reply to Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng) yesterday.
Tan had asked about the compliance rate and findings since the policy took effect, as well as its impact on transparency, healthy competition and medicine prices for patients.
Community pharmacies recorded the highest satisfactory rate at 73.1 per cent, involving 2,628 of 3,595 premises.
Private hospitals followed at 61.4 per cent (78 of 127), while private medical clinics recorded 57.2 per cent (972 of 1,699).
Dental clinics had the lowest rate at 43.6 per cent (219 of 502).
Mandatory medicine price display took effect on May 1, 2025, under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking for Medicines) Order 2025.
Several medical and dental practitioner associations filed for a judicial review of the requirement in July last year.

Title: US$14bil arms sale 'up to' Trump, Taiwan official says
Article:
TAIPEI: The timing of Washington's US$14 billion arms sales package to Taiwan is "very much up to" President Donald Trump and will not be affected by the US midterm results, according to a Taiwanese government official.
Taiwan has been waiting months for Trump to approve the record sale of weapons and equipment that the island says it needs to strengthen its defence capabilities to deter a potential Chinese attack.
Beijing claims the island democracy is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.
Trump has stalled the arms sale, saying in May it could be used as a bargaining chip with China, as the two superpowers tried to ease trade tensions.
"When it comes to time, I think it's very much up to... President Trump," said Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi.
Taiwan enjoys "very strong bipartisan support" from Congress, and this month's midterm results, which saw Democrats win control of the House and Senate, would not affect the timing, Chen said.
The Trump administration had to consider "many factors" when it came to arms sales to Taiwan, including the Middle East war.
"We respect that, but at the same time, we express that we really have an urgent need for those capabilities," Chen said.
Patriot missiles, an automated command and control system and a 360-degree air defence radar system are among the items in the US$14 billion package.
Chen said Taiwan had "very good direct communication" with the Trump administration and "we are reassured that that will not change".
"This could be just a matter of time before" the sale is approved, either as one package or in smaller parcels, he said.
Taiwan 'structurally important'
Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping for the third and fourth time this year at an Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen this week and at the G20 in the United States in December.
While Taiwan has been on the agenda at previous talks between the rival leaders, Chen brushed off concerns about the upcoming meetings.
"We are very confident and very comfortable with our relationship with the US and with other like-minded partners," Chen said.
"We are structurally important, and our people (are) committed to our own defence. I think this (is) what matters the most," he said.
"And Taiwan stands in the middle of the whole AI revolution. I think that now almost every leader in the world understands the situation."
Taiwan is a powerhouse in the global semiconductor industry, producing nearly all of the most advanced chips for companies including Nvidia and Apple.
After Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who US intelligence agencies believe is spying for Beijing, Chen said the case underlines the need to be "very vigilant about China".
China is "very aggressive" when it comes to stealing intellectual property and technology to get around export controls, Chen said.
Huang, who regularly visited Taiwan to see Nvidia's clients, including TSMC, and had been seen in the capital Taipei with the Chinese woman, would be welcome back to the island, Chen said.
"He certainly will be welcome but I think... every business leader in the world has to learn this lesson that China is trying to poach your trade secrets," he said.
"They are going to arrange (a) spy in your life so that they can get easier access."
Beijing has rejected the allegations as "entirely baseless".
China is in a race for tech dominance against the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips.
Taiwan has long accused China of carrying out espionage activities on the island, including targeting its tech sector.

Title: Australia to make backpackers do extra rural work to meet labour crunch
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia said on Tuesday it will require tourists on working holiday visas to complete extra work in rural areas, as the government attempts to balance a reduction in migration with a shortage of labour in its farming and hospitality sectors.
Australia's Working Holiday Maker programme — a popular rite of passage for young people from more than a dozen countries — will now require applicants to complete four months of rural work to remain in the country for a second year, up from the current three months.
"Working holiday makers make an important contribution to our economy, especially in agriculture, tourism and hospitality and in regional Australia," Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said.
"But when demand grows too fast, the government needs the tools to manage the programme properly."
Rural employers in Australia are heavily reliant on backpackers to fill seasonal roles.
Under the programme for 18-to-35-year-olds, Australia grants a one-year working holiday visa, extendable for a second and third year if the backpackers undertake regional work.
Backpackers typically work as nannies, waiters and in farming, among other retail and hospitality jobs.
Under a 2021 carve-out agreed by previous governments in both countries, the rural work rules do not apply to UK backpackers, which has led to a surge of British arrivals in Australia and a shortage of workers in regional areas.
Australia has already announced curbs on foreign students bringing partners and children to accompany them while they study, as well as a ballot system for backpackers, amid growing debate in the country over high migration levels.

Title: Malaysia investment approvals jump 20.7pct to RM350.4bil in nine months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has attracted RM350.4 billion in approved investments across the services, manufacturing and primary sectors in the first nine months of 2026, up 20.7 per cent from RM290.3 billion a year earlier.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said the 4,387 approved projects are expected to generate 152,090 jobs upon full implementation.
Foreign investments accounted for RM212.3 billion, or 60.6 per cent of total approvals, while domestic investments stood at RM138.1 billion.
The United States was the largest foreign investment source, contributing RM60 billion, more than five times the RM11.3 billion recorded in the corresponding period last year.
China followed with RM38.6 billion, Singapore RM38.5 billion, Japan RM24.4 billion and Australia RM12.6 billion.
Collectively, the five countries contributed RM174.1 billion, or 82 per cent of total foreign investment approvals.
The nine-month investment total represents 81.3 per cent of the revised RM431.1 billion approved for the whole of 2025.
Mida chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the performance demonstrated Malaysia's continued appeal despite global economic uncertainty.
He said the focus was on ensuring investments translated into high-value employment, stronger industrial capabilities and opportunities for local talent.
"These industries deepen our industrial capabilities, strengthen Malaysia's position in global value chains and create well-paying career opportunities for our people.
"Mida is also working closely with industry and education partners to ensure talent development keeps pace with investor needs. Investing in skills and higher-quality jobs is key to a stronger industrial ecosystem," he said in a statement today.
SERVICES LEAD INVESTMENT INFLOWS
The services sector attracted the largest share of investments at RM219.1 billion, accounting for 62.5 per cent of total approvals.
This represented a 14.2 per cent increase from RM191.7 billion in the same period last year, with 2,993 projects expected to generate 59,273 jobs.
Information and communications led the sector with RM133.5 billion, followed by real estate at RM47.9 billion and support services at RM19.3 billion.
Data centre and cloud computing projects accounted for RM123.5 billion across 86 projects, up 44.5 per cent year-on-year.
The projects represented 35.2 per cent of total approved investments, compared with 29.4 per cent in the corresponding period last year.
MANUFACTURING REBOUNDS
The manufacturing sector secured RM106.3 billion across 1,353 projects, marking a 13.3 per cent increase in investment value and a 53.1 per cent rise in project numbers.
The performance marked a turnaround from the 25.1 per cent decline in investment value recorded in the first half of 2026, supported by third-quarter approvals involving optical transceivers for AI data centres and liquefied natural gas processing.
The electrical and electronics (E&E) industry led manufacturing investments with RM40.8 billion, up 85.3 per cent year-on-year.
Other major contributors included petroleum products and petrochemicals at RM13.2 billion, machinery and equipment (RM9.4 billion), basic metal products (RM6.7 billion) and food manufacturing (RM6.4 billion).
Manufacturing projects are expected to generate 92,489 jobs, of which 72,111, or 78 per cent, will go to Malaysians.
Of the 34,529 managerial, technical, supervisory and skilled positions, 92.4 per cent are allocated to Malaysians.
Some 16,607 positions are expected to offer monthly salaries of at least RM5,000.
PRIMARY SECTOR SURGES
The primary sector recorded RM25 billion in approved investments, surging 420 per cent from RM4.8 billion a year earlier.
The amount also exceeded the sector's full-year 2025 investment total of RM14.2 billion by 76.9 per cent.
Domestic investments contributed RM13.9 billion, while foreign investments stood at RM11.1 billion.
Mining accounted for RM24.8 billion, mainly involving oil and gas exploration and development, while agriculture contributed about RM300 million.
JOHOR TOPS INVESTMENT DESTINATIONS
Johor emerged as the largest investment destination with RM99.7 billion in approvals, followed by Selangor at RM87.9 billion, Penang (RM41.1 billion), Kuala Lumpur (RM37.3 billion) and Sabah (RM19.5 billion).
Together, the five states accounted for 81.5 per cent of total approved investments.
Johor's approvals were driven by RM68.3 billion in services, mainly information and communications, and RM31.2 billion in manufacturing, led by E&E.
Selangor recorded the highest number of projects at 1,302, which are expected to create 34,971 jobs.
Mida said 87.4 per cent of the 6,202 manufacturing projects approved between 2021 and September 2026 had reached various stages of implementation, including production, factory construction or machinery installation.
As of October, Mida had 223 proposed projects worth RM41.2 billion under its purview, comprising 119 manufacturing projects valued at RM18.6 billion and 104 services projects worth RM22.6 billion.
It was also discussing potential investments worth RM60.5 billion.

Title: Trump, Li Qiang, Modi join Asean leaders as Philippines hosts summit finale
Article:
MANILA: The Philippines takes centre stage as Asean leaders and key global figures gather for crucial talks on the final day of the 49th Asean Summit.
United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in Manila at 5.30pm local time, making him the last world leader scheduled to arrive for the summit.
His arrival is scheduled half an hour after the closing ceremony begins at 5pm. The ceremony is expected to end at 5.45pm.
Trump is also expected to deliver remarks at a dinner with Asean leaders scheduled for 8.25pm.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang arrived on Sunday to attend the Asean-China Summit, while Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined the Asean-India Summit the following day.
Several key meetings with dialogue partners are scheduled for the final day.
They include the 29th Asean Plus Three (APT) Summit, which began at 8.30am, followed by the fourth Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) Leaders' Meeting at 10.15am.
The 29th Asean-Japan Summit is scheduled for 11.15am, followed by the 13th Mekong-Japan Summit at 12.30pm and the 23rd Asean-India Summit at 1.15pm.
The programme continues with the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) at 2.30pm, bringing together regional leaders and dialogue partners to discuss issues of mutual interest.
The day's proceedings will include the closing ceremony of the 49th Asean Summit, during which the Philippines will formally hand over the Asean chairmanship to Singapore for 2027.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, as Asean chairman, is scheduled to deliver remarks at the ceremony.
The Asean-United States Special Summit will follow the closing ceremony, bringing the day's meetings to a close.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who returned to Malaysia yesterday to receive French President Emmanuel Macron, is scheduled to arrive back in Manila at 4.25pm today to attend the special summit and a dinner hosted by Marcos.

Title: Malaysia's construction sector builds on growth momentum
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's construction sector continues to expand in the third quarter of 2026, supported by strong private-sector activity, growing data centre developments and sustained demand for non-residential buildings.
Construction work done rose 9.0 per cent year-on-year to RM49.5 billion in the quarter, marking the 15th consecutive quarter of expansion, MBSB Research said, based on the Department of Statistics data.
The value of work done also increased 3.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter, bringing the total for the first nine months of 2026 to RM143.9 billion, up 8.8 per cent from a year earlier.
Non-residential buildings recorded the strongest growth, rising 21.1 per cent to RM15.7 billion, while special trades increased 13.2 per cent to RM6.2 billion.
The private sector remained the main growth driver, with construction work done rising 12.7 per cent to RM33.3 billion, compared with a 2.2 per cent expansion in public-sector activity.
Selangor and Johor accounted for 43.2 per cent of nationwide construction work done, reflecting the concentration of data centre and advanced industrial developments in both states.
MBSB Research said the latest figures indicated that data centre contract awards were translating into physical construction activity, although public infrastructure projects had yet to provide a comparable boost.
On the infrastructure front, the RM2.69 billion contract for the second civil and major infrastructure works package (CMC2) of the Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) Mutiara Line brought the value of the project's three main packages to RM13.65 billion.
The package, awarded to the China Communications Construction Co-TRC-Ufuk consortium, covers a 5.5km connection from Macallum to Penang Sentral, including a 3.05km sea-crossing bridge linking Penang island to the mainland's rail and bus network.
This follows the RM7.93 billion CMC1 package secured by Gamuda Bhd-led SRS consortium, while the RM3.03 billion systems package was awarded to the MRCB-Theta Edge consortium.
With overall construction progress at about 16 per cent, MBSB Research expects Gamuda's billings to increase as civil works gather pace, while MRCB's contribution should accelerate following the initial design and mobilisation stages.
Looking ahead, MBSB Research said the next major public-sector opportunities include RM9 billion to RM12 billion worth of water infrastructure projects, comprising Northern Perak Water, Langat 2 Phase 2 and Sungai Rasau Phase 2.
Johor's proposed RM7 billion to RM8 billion elevated autonomous rapid transit system also represents a medium-term opportunity, pending greater clarity on funding and procurement.
On construction material costs, the firm said steel prices remained manageable, with average steel bar prices rising 4.1 per cent month-on-month to RM2,210 per tonne in October, although they remained 6.4 per cent below the May peak.
Bulk cement prices fell 1.2 per cent month-on-month to RM397 per tonne, while coal procurement costs stood at between US$80 and US$90 per tonne, posing a margin challenge amid softer average selling prices.
MBSB Research estimated that every sustained US$10 per tonne movement in coal costs could change Malayan Cement Bhd's annual earnings by about five to six per cent and its earnings before interest and tax margin by 130 basis points, assuming limited cost pass-through.
Despite cost pressures and uncertainty surrounding tighter US chip controls, the research house maintained a positive outlook on the construction sector.
It cited record data centre contract awards of RM18.24 billion in 2026, nearly double the previous year's level, alongside continued growth in construction activity.
The RM430 billion development expenditure allocation under the 13th Malaysia Plan also provides a broader medium-term opportunity, spanning transport, water, power grid and East Malaysian infrastructure projects.
MBSB Research named Gamuda, Sunway Contruction Group Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd as its top picks, with buy recommendations and target prices of RM5.60, RM9.28 and RM3.32 respectively.

Title: US chip curbs put data centre projects in focus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's construction players with heavy exposure to data centre projects could face greater uncertainty following tighter United States (US) restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, although existing projects are unlikely to be derailed immediately.
MBSB Research said the new US Commerce Department rules, which seek to prevent restricted users from remotely accessing advanced American chips through overseas data centres, could raise compliance requirements and slow the rollout of future projects in Malaysia.
It said the immediate impact will likely be on graphics processing unit (GPU) deployment and capacity activation, with construction demand affected only if delays weakened tenant commitments or postponed subsequent development phases.
Projects backed by established US hyperscalers are expected to be better positioned to meet the new requirements.
Facilities relying on Chinese AI customers or less transparent GPU-as-a-Service arrangements could face longer licensing and customer-verification processes.
MBSB Research said exposure to data centre projects varied among major construction companies, with Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) having the highest concentration, while Gamuda Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd had more diversified order books.
SunCon's outstanding data centre works were estimated at RM10.5 billion to RM11 billion, equivalent to 78-82 per cent of its RM13.4 billion order book.
IJM's remaining data centre works were estimated at RM1.8 billion to RM2.2 billion, representing 12 to 15 per cent of its RM14.5 billion order book.
Kerjaya Prospek's maiden data centre contract worth RM858 million accounted for 12 to 14 per cent of its RM6 billion backlog.
Gamuda had estimated data centre exposure of RM6.5 billion to RM7 billion, or a smaller 9.8 to 10.6 per cent of its RM66 billion order book, providing greater diversification through its infrastructure portfolio.
Despite the regulatory uncertainty, commitments from major US hyperscalers continue to underpin Malaysia's data centre investment pipeline.
Google plans to invest US$15 billion in Malaysia in 2027 and 2028, including additional campuses in Selangor and Negri Sembilan, alongside more than 1GW of clean-energy capacity and related water infrastructure.
Microsoft has committed US$2.2 billion over four years and is developing its SEA3 facility in Johor as its second Malaysian cloud region, while Amazon Web Services plans to invest US$6.2 billion through 2038.
However, MBSB Research cautioned that tighter chip controls and greater scrutiny of returns from AI investments could prompt hyperscalers to phase their capital expenditure more cautiously, particularly for expansion phases that have yet to be committed.
The firm said existing awarded projects and visible US-backed opportunities over the next 12 months should remain largely intact, although tighter controls could delay subsequent development phases and slow new contract awards.
It maintained a positive outlook on the construction sector, with Gamuda, SunCon and IJM as its top picks, carrying buy recommendations and target prices of RM5.60, RM9.28 and RM3.32 respectively.

Title: Macron accorded state welcome at Dataran Merdeka
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron, who is on a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday, was accorded a state welcome at Dataran Merdeka here this morning.
Macron, accompanied by his wife Brigitte Macron, arrived at 9.30am and was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
Also present were both Deputy Prime Ministers, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
The ceremony began with the French and Malaysian national anthems, performed by the Central Band of the Royal Malay Regiment (RAMD) under the baton of Captain Muhamad Fauzee Japar.
Macron then inspected a guard of honour comprising three officers and 103 other ranks from the First Battalion of RAMD, commanded by Major Adibadiuezshah Ahmad.
Notably, the welcome was held at the historic Dataran Merdeka, a site synonymous with the nation's struggle for independence and one of the capital's defining landmarks, rather than in Putrajaya or at Istana Negara, where previous official ceremonies for foreign leaders have been staged.
This is Macron's first official trip to Malaysia since he assumed the French presidency in May 2017.
The visit is expected to open a new chapter in Malaysia-France relations, with both countries seeking to elevate their existing ties to a strategic partnership.
Priority areas of cooperation include defence and security, critical minerals, energy transition, aeronautics and aerospace, AI, cybersecurity and semiconductors.
The visit builds on the momentum from Anwar's official trip to France in July 2025, the first by a Malaysian head of government to the country in 15 years.
France is Malaysia's 10th-largest trading partner and its third-largest within the European Union, with bilateral trade reaching €4.7 billion (approximately RM21.23 billion) in 2025, up 11 per cent from 2024.

Title: Shell's Rosmari-Marjoram gas fields start production
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Shell Bhd has started production from the Rosmari and Marjoram gas fields located 220 kilometres off the coast of Sarawak.
Gas produced from Rosmari-Marjoram will be piped to a new onshore gas plant in Bintulu, where it will be processed and fed to the Petronas LNG Complex.
Shell upstream president Perer Costello said the company is proud of its long and successful history in Malaysia.
"We have strong expertise in this basin, and the start-up of Rosmari-Marjoram contributes to production growth into the 2030s.
"This project builds on decades of experience to bring new gas supply online efficiently and competitively," Costello said in a statement.
Rosmari-Marjoram's offshore platform is powered by solar panels, with back-up diesel generators available when needed.
The onshore plant draws on the predominantly hydropower-based local electricity grid, supplemented by renewable energy certificates to achieve 100 per cent renewable power.
Country chair and senior vice president for upstream Siti Sulaiman said the start of production from Rosmari-Marjoram is an important milestone for Shell in Malaysia and a reflection of the strong partnership it has with Petroliam Nasional Bhd, the federal government and Sarawak.
"We remain committed to helping meet Malaysia's growing energy needs and contributing to the nation's economic progress through investments that are competitive and resilient."
Shell drilled Malaysia's first oil well in 1910 and has been producing gas offshore since 1982.
In addition to Rosmari-Marjoram, Shell has interests in a number of producing fields off the coast of Sarawak including Timi and Gorek and is exploring other potential opportunities in the basin.

Title: CAP warns of rising old-age poverty risk
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Low wages, inadequate retirement savings and rising living costs are leaving retirees financially vulnerable, with the risk of old-age poverty growing, the Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has warned.
The country became an ageing society in 2021, when people aged 65 and above accounted for seven per cent of the population. Their share is projected to reach 14 per cent by 2048, when it is expected to become an aged nation.
CAP president Mohideen Abdul Kader said the country needed to overhaul its retirement, healthcare and wage policies to prepare for the challenges of an ageing population.
He said many Malaysians who entered the workforce in the 1980s were approaching retirement with inadequate Employees Provident Fund savings because of historically low wages and withdrawals for housing and education.
Rising costs of food, utilities, transport and healthcare, coupled with chronic illnesses, had further weakened their financial security.
As a result, many older people were increasingly dependent on their children, public healthcare and government assistance, he said.
This also placed pressure on the sandwich generation, which had to support both children and ageing parents, leaving little room for its own retirement savings.
Mohideen warned that a shrinking workforce could slow economic growth and reduce tax revenue, while increasing public spending on healthcare and elderly care.
CAP proposed four measures to address the challenge: higher wages and productivity, a job-matching centre for retirees, greater emphasis on preventive healthcare and stronger social safety nets.
He said higher lifetime earnings were essential to help workers accumulate sufficient retirement savings.
A one-stop skills-matching centre could connect healthy retirees with flexible or part-time employment, providing additional income while helping address labour shortages.
He also called for greater emphasis on healthy ageing to prevent chronic diseases and ease pressure on public hospitals, as well as targeted financial assistance to protect older people from poverty without placing excessive strain on government finances.
Mohideen welcomed the Dewan Rakyat's passage of the National Trust Fund Bill 2026 in July, saying stronger controls on withdrawals and governance standards would help safeguard national wealth for future generations.
"The generation now entering retirement cannot realistically rebuild decades of insufficient savings," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan scrambles jets after two suspected Russian aircraft enter airspace
Article:
TOKYO: Japan said on Tuesday it scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace, and lodged a "very stern protest" with Moscow.
The aircraft entered Japan's airspace close to Okinoshima, in the southwestern area of Fukuoka, shortly after 4am on Tuesday (1900 GMT Monday).
Japan's Self-Defence Force scrambled fighter jets to warn the planes, top government spokesman Minoru Kihara said.
"The violation of our national airspace by Russian aircraft is not only a grave infringement of our country's sovereignty, but also a threat to our security and is completely unacceptable," Kihara said.
"We lodged a very stern protest with Russia through diplomatic channels and strongly demanded measures to prevent any recurrence."
Relations with Moscow have soured in recent weeks following the arrest of a Japanese journalist on spying allegations and the seizure of Japan Tobacco's Russian assets.

Title: Malayan Flour earnings recovery set to continue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Flour Mills Bhd is expected to sustain its earnings recovery, supported by improved flour milling efficiency, favourable input costs and stronger margins in its integrated poultry business.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) analyst Chye Wen Fei said the company's earnings prospects remained positive.
Malayan Flour's poultry operations is expected to benefit from a better product mix as it shifts towards higher-value offerings, alongside capacity expansion across its upstream and downstream businesses.
"We remain constructive of Malayan Flour's earnings prospects, underpinned by improved operating efficiency at its flour milling operations in Malaysia and Vietnam, favourable input cost dynamics within its flour milling operations and margin expansion at the integrated poultry segment," she said in a note.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on Malayan Flour with an unchanged target price of 93 sen, valuing the company at seven times its mid-financial year 2027 core earnings per share of 13.3 sen.
Chye said the company's third-quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) core earnings rose 8.9 per cent to RM39.4 million, bringing its nine-month (9M) core earnings to RM124.1 million, up 21.3 per cent from a year earlier.
The nine-month performance accounted for 78.3 per cent of HLIB's full-year earnings forecast, placing the results within the research house's expectations.
However, Q3 FY26 core earnings declined 7.4 per cent quarter-on-quarter, as improvements in the flour and grain trading segment and poultry integration business were offset by losses from its Indonesian flour operations.
The Indonesian business was affected by lower sales volume and contribution margins, Chye said.
On a yearly basis, higher sales volume and contribution margins in the flour and grain trading segment supported earnings growth.
The poultry integration business, operated through its 51 per cent-owned joint venture Dindings Tyson Sdn Bhd, also recorded a stronger contribution, driven by higher sales volume, improved margins and increased fair value gains on biological assets.
For 9M 2026, earnings improved across all segments, including joint ventures.
The poultry integration business more than tripled its contribution to RM27 million, compared with RM8 million in the corresponding period last year, reflecting stronger sales volume and contribution margins, alongside fair value gains on biological assets.
Meanwhile, the flour and grain trading segment recorded higher earnings on stronger sales volume, although the improvement was partly offset by higher operating costs, which HLIB attributed to increased raw material costs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang Hospital services unaffected by ambulance fire
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Operations at Penang Hospital's Emergency and Trauma Department remain unaffected following a fire involving a Civil Defence Force ambulance.
The Penang Health Department said medical services continued as normal.
The fire broke out at 1pm in the engine compartment of a
Toyota Hiace ambulance
parked outside the department.
The 32-year-old female driver escaped unharmed.
The fire broke out after the ambulance crew had transferred an emergency patient to the department.
"Thick smoke was seen coming from the vehicle, but quick action by emergency healthcare staff and the ambulance crew using fire extinguishers brought the blaze under control before it could spread," the department said in a statement posted on Facebook.
