Title: Malaysia has 133,400 registered Rohingya refugees and asylum seekers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 133,400 Rohingya refugees and asylum seekers were registered with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Malaysia as at Sept 30.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said 6,294 Rohingya were being held at immigration detention depots nationwide as at Oct 31.
They accounted for part of the 11,208 Myanmar nationals in detention, based on Immigration Department records.
He said repatriating foreigners, particularly those without valid travel or identity documents, required cooperation from their countries of origin to identify them, verify their nationality and issue the necessary travel documents.
"As at Oct 31, a total of 12,176 Myanmar nationals had been repatriated this year, including 1,476 detainees sent home on Sept 29 in a large-scale operation aboard a Myanmar Navy vessel.
"However, these repatriation figures are based on nationality confirmed by the country of origin, not ethnicity," he said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Parliament website.
He was responding to Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong), who asked for the latest number of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia, including those repatriated to Myanmar this year.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry continued to work with the National Security Council and Foreign Ministry to coordinate negotiations with the Myanmar government.
The efforts focused on speeding up nationality verification, issuing travel documents and securing the acceptance of returning Myanmar nationals by their country of origin.
"This cooperation is important to ensure repatriations are carried out safely, in an orderly and responsible manner, in accordance with the laws and procedures in force," he said.
Saifuddin said identified methods included bringing foreigners into Malaysia illegally through land and sea routes that were not gazetted as official entry points.
The movements involved regional migrant smuggling syndicates that arranged cross-border journeys from Myanmar or Bangladesh, including through transit countries, before bringing them into Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flood damage cost Selangor RM52.9m last year, more than double the 2024 figure
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — Flood losses in Selangor rose to RM52.9 million in 2025 from RM22.6 million the previous year, said Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi.
Citing the Selangor State Flood Loss Value Statistics for 2024 and 2025 compiled by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) Selangor, he said the losses comprised RM15.3 million in damage to residences, RM4 million to vehicles and RM1 million to business premises.
Mohd Najwan said agricultural losses and infrastructure damage stood at RM9.6 million and RM26.6 million, respectively.
“Based on the Special Report on the Impact of Floods in Malaysia 2025 published by DOSM, total flood losses nationwide in 2025 amounted to RM636.9 million, compared with RM933.4 million in 2024.
“All states in Malaysia were affected by floods, with Terengganu recording the highest losses at RM89.2 million.
“This was followed by Kelantan and Johor, which recorded losses of RM88.5 million and RM72.1 million, respectively,” he said at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
He was responding to Danial Al-Rashid Haron Aminar Rashid (PH-Batu Tiga), who asked for the estimated annual economic losses arising from incidents such as floods, fires and others.
Najwan said the state government is committed to improving the quality of aid delivery, particularly in addressing the issue of recurring flood victims, and that the matter would be discussed with the State Disaster Management Unit. — Bernama

Title: Over 13,000 deepfakes taken down since 2024, including 1,178 targeting political leaders, Parliament told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Platform providers removed 13,883 deepfake items between January 1, 2024, and October 31 this year following takedown requests by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) based on public complaints, Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil told Parliament today.
Of these, 1,178 items involved political leaders, Fahmi said when outlining regulatory and enforcement measures against artificial intelligence (AI) misuse.
He said that under the Risk Mitigation Code, which took effect on June 1 this year, licensed service providers are required to establish mechanisms to identify, assess and address harmful content.
The code also requires AI-generated or manipulated images, audio and video likely to be mistaken for authentic content to be clearly labelled, and that users be given accessible reporting tools.
“On the prevention front, the government, through the MCMC, is also implementing the Safe Internet campaign to raise public awareness and digital literacy, particularly in identifying deepfake content, identity impersonation, and AI-generated false information,” he said during Question Time.
“The campaign also emphasises the importance of verifying information before believing or sharing it, to prevent the public from falling victim to online scams and information manipulation.”
On enforcement, Fahmi said the MCMC investigated 61 cases involving AI misuse under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) between January 1, 2025, and October 31 this year.
Of these, 10 cases were brought to court, while compounds totalling RM755,000 were issued in seven cases and 17 warning letters were served.
Six of the 10 court cases have been decided, with fines totalling RM19,500.
He did not say what action was taken on the remaining 27 cases.

Title: No sticker, but don’t forget to renew: JPJ seized 35,555 vehicles over expired road tax since 2023
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has seized 35,555 vehicles since 2023 for being driven with expired motor vehicle licences (LKM) or road tax, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
The Transport Ministry (MOT) said 1,608,238 P22 summons notices were also issued during the same period to motorists caught driving vehicles with expired road tax.
It said the digitalisation of road tax, introduced on February 10, 2023, was aimed at supporting the national digitalisation agenda while reducing printing costs and congestion at service counters.
“The introduction of e-LKM is primarily aimed at supporting the country’s digitalisation efforts while reducing government spending on printing road tax stickers, easing congestion at service counters and allowing motorists to renew their road tax through the MyJPJ application and other digital channels,” said the ministry in a written reply to a question from Datuk Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu).
It said that although motorists were no longer required to display physical road tax stickers, vehicle owners were still responsible for ensuring that their road tax was renewed and remained valid.
The ministry said enforcement officers could verify road tax validity digitally through JPJ’s system, while action could be taken under the Road Transport Act 1987 against those driving vehicles with expired road tax on public roads. — Bernama

Title: Anwar welcomes Macron at historic Dataran Merdeka ceremony
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — French President Emmanuel Macron, on a two-day official visit to Malaysia beginning yesterday, was accorded a state welcome at Dataran Merdeka here this morning.
Macron, accompanied by his wife Brigitte Macron, arrived at 9.30 am and was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
Also present were both Deputy Prime Ministers, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
The ceremony began with the French and Malaysian national anthems, performed by the Central Band of the Royal Malay Regiment (RAMD) under the baton of Captain Muhamad Fauzee Japar.
Macron then inspected a guard of honour comprising three officers and 103 other ranks from the First Battalion of RAMD, commanded by Major Adibadiuezshah Ahmad.
Notably, the welcome was held at the historic Dataran Merdeka, a site synonymous with the nation’s struggle for independence and one of the capital’s defining landmarks, rather than in Putrajaya or at Istana Negara, where previous official ceremonies for foreign leaders have been staged.
This is Macron’s first official trip to Malaysia since he assumed the French presidency in May 2017.
It is expected to open a new chapter in Malaysia-France relations, with both countries seeking to elevate their existing ties to a Strategic Partnership.
Priority areas of cooperation include defence and security, critical minerals, energy transition, aeronautics and aerospace, AI, cybersecurity and semiconductors.
The visit builds on the momentum from Anwar’s official trip to France in July 2025, the first by a Malaysian head of government to the country in 15 years.
France is Malaysia’s 10th-largest trading partner and its third-largest within the European Union, with bilateral trade reaching €4.7 billion (approximately RM21.23 billion) in 2025, up 11 per cent from 2024. — Bernama

Title: Government to table White Paper on ageing population challenges and opportunities
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — A White Paper on Malaysia’s preparations to become an aged nation is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on Dec 2, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said.
He said Malaysia entered ageing-nation status in 2021 and is expected to become an aged nation by 2048 before reaching super-aged status in 2060.
He said plans for this demographic shift should not be viewed solely through the lens of managing senior citizens’ welfare, but must also include equipping future generations for structural changes in the economy and society.
“Preparations for becoming an aged nation are not merely about identifying existing gaps that need to be improved, but also about preparing future generations to face this situation,” he said at the Economy Ministry’s monthly assembly today. Also present was Deputy Minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shahar Abdullah.
He noted that Malaysia’s transition from an ageing nation to an aged nation will be relatively brief, about 27 years, necessitating early groundwork to ensure the demographic shift does not create a generational divide.
Future changes in population and workforce numbers will also affect the country’s economic capacity, including the need to ensure that senior citizens can sustain their livelihoods as well as remain capable of contributing to society and the economy, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
In addition, he said the government is also examining the economic potential that can be unlocked from the demographic shift, including through the silver economy concept.
He said areas that will be given attention include job opportunities for senior citizens, ageing-related economic opportunities, the care economy, and efforts to make communities and cities more age-friendly.
“How we create economic opportunities and potential is tied to these changing dynamics. In terms of theme, we are indeed adopting the silver economy,” he said.
The silver economy refers to a market system of products and services designed specifically to meet the needs, wants and purchasing power of senior citizens and retirees, in line with Malaysia’s transition towards ageing-nation status.
Senior citizens’ welfare and care should not be viewed as a zero-sum game but must instead be assessed in terms of the benefits it can deliver to the country and to families, he said.
Improving the welfare of senior citizens has the potential to generate returns for the national economy if supported by appropriate structures and systems, he said.
At the same time, investment in the younger generation must remain a priority and form part of the nation’s preparations for demographic change, he added.
“Investment in the younger generation cannot be sidelined; it must serve as the foundation for preparing ourselves for an aged nation,” he said.
He said the White Paper will examine the issue more comprehensively before the government rolls out a full blueprint for addressing an aged nation thereafter.
He said population ageing transcends political and generational interests, as it is tied to Malaysia’s ability to strike a balance between demographic change and the country’s economic needs. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected in parts of Perak, Pahang, Sabah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in Perak, Pahang and Sabah until 1 pm today.
In a statement today, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the affected areas in Perak are Hulu Perak and Kuala Kangsar, while in Pahang, they involve Pekan and Kuantan.
In Sabah, the forecast covers the West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud, Tuaran and Kota Kinabalu), Sandakan (Telupid, Paitan, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: BMI: Higher living costs set to squeeze Malaysian households’   purchasing power
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysian households are expected to face growing price pressures in 2027 as inflation remains elevated and economic growth moderates, according to a new consumer outlook by Fitch Solutions unit, BMI.
BMI said consumers are likely to encounter a more challenging spending environment next year after revising its inflation forecast for Malaysia to 2.0 per cent from 1.8 per cent previously. Elevated prices are expected to continue weighing on household purchasing power and restrain discretionary spending.
The report noted that inflation remains above pre-pandemic levels and that the pressure on households would be compounded by high household debt and related debt-servicing costs. It also forecast limited monetary policy relief, with Bank Negara Malaysia expected to maintain its policy rate at 2.75 per cent until the first quarter of 2027.
At the same time, BMI expects Malaysia's economic growth to ease in the third quarter of 2026. The research house forecast real GDP growth to slow to 5.2 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter from 6.0 per cent in the preceding quarter, citing mixed high-frequency economic indicators.
According to the report, export growth strengthened from 45.5 per cent year-on-year in June to 54.5 per cent in September, while retail sales growth moderated from 4.2 per cent in June to 3.8 per cent in August.
BMI also said headline inflation edged lower from 1.9 per cent year-on-year in August to 1.8 per cent in September, but is expected to move closer to 2.0 per cent in October due to rising housing and food costs.
Despite the expected pressures, the report projected household spending to remain resilient. Real household spending growth is forecast to ease only marginally to 4.07 per cent in 2027 from 4.08 per cent in 2026.
BMI said it would also be monitoring the release of Malaysia's third-quarter GDP data and inflation figures as indicators of the country's consumer outlook going into 2027.

Title: Malaysians lost RM6.95b to online scams since 2023, Home Ministry says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysians lost RM6.95 billion to online scams between 2023 and August 2026, according to the latest figures disclosed by the Home Ministry in Parliament.
In a written parliamentary reply dated November 1, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police recorded 181,750 online fraud cases over the nearly four-year period, with both case numbers and losses surging in 2025.
“In terms of losses, the total amount recorded for the period from 2023 to August 2026 stood at RM6.95 billion. Losses in 2023 totalled RM1.22 billion, rising to RM1.57 billion in 2024 and RM2.97 billion in 2025,” he said.
Between January and August 2026, victims lost RM1.18 billion, the reply added.
Case numbers rose slightly from 34,495 in 2023 to 35,368 in 2024, before nearly doubling to 66,204 in 2025.
From January to August 2026, police logged another 45,683 cases, Saifuddin said.
By category, telecommunications scams recorded the most cases at 69,195, followed by e-commerce fraud at 47,221. Love scams accounted for the fewest, at 3,540 cases.
The ministry said it viewed the escalation of online fraud seriously, noting that commercial cybercrime remains one of the country’s main law enforcement challenges because of the scale of losses suffered by victims.

Title: Royal assent needed before MB resignation takes effect, says Palace
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace has clarified that Datuk Ismail Lasim remains Menteri Besar pending royal assent, stressing that any resignation only takes effect after it is accepted by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan in accordance with the state constitution.
In a statement today, the palace said it had taken note of a statement issued by Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir on Nov 16 regarding Ismail's purported resignation from the post.
The palace said the statement appeared to be based on a copy of a resignation letter that was in Zambry's possession.
Under the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution, any resignation by a Menteri Besar must be submitted to the Yang Dipertuan Besar and only becomes effective upon receiving royal consent, it said.
According to the statement, the resignation letter was delivered to Istana Hinggap in Seremban at 12.16am today by an individual who identified himself as Hamidi from the law firm Shahrul Hamidi & Haziq.
The palace also revealed that Ismail had earlier been granted an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar after making a request to do so.
It said the Ruler's private secretary informed Ismail via WhatsApp at 8.38pm on Nov 16 that his request had been approved, and that he had acknowledged receipt of the message.
The audience has been scheduled for 10am on Nov 20.
According to the palace, the approval for the audience was conveyed about 80 minutes before Zambry's social media posting announcing the resignation.
The palace further said it had yet to verify the authenticity of the resignation letter, which Zambry had stated was signed by Ismail.
The clarification comes amid heightened political attention in Negeri Sembilan following the announcement that Ismail had stepped down as Menteri Besar.

Title: Lim Guan Eng: Indonesia must pay for haze losses or permit regional firefighting force
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng has urged Indonesia to either compensate Malaysia for losses arising from this year’s haze crisis or agree to the formation of a permanent trans-boundary firefighting task force with the authority to enter Indonesian forests immediately to combat fires.
In a statement today, Lim said Malaysia should accept the apology offered by Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto to Malaysia and Singapore over the prolonged haze episode in the spirit of good neighbourly relations and ASEAN solidarity.
However, he said Indonesia could not disclaim responsibility for the duration and impact of the crisis, which he said had been worsened by this year’s Super El Nino conditions.
Lim claimed that Malaysia had suffered welfare losses of RM8 billion linked to health impacts and economic losses of RM5 billion as a result of the haze.
He cited a study commissioned by the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers, which estimated that severe air pollution could reduce international tourist arrivals by up to eight per cent and jeopardise the Visit Malaysia 2026 campaign, with potential losses of up to RM5 billion in tourism-related gross domestic product.
According to Lim, the estimated RM8 billion in welfare losses reflected the economic cost associated with premature mortality risks and was linked to an estimated 1,700 premature deaths among Malaysians.
He said measures such as the use of air purifiers were essential during severe haze episodes and reiterated his earlier proposal for a RM1,000 tax rebate for the purchase of air purifiers to help protect vulnerable groups, particularly young children and senior citizens.
Lim said that if Indonesia was unable to provide compensation, it should agree to the establishment of a Permanent Trans-Boundary Haze Relief Task Force comprising trained personnel capable of undertaking immediate firefighting operations in Indonesian forests.
He said such a mechanism was necessary to prevent haze from becoming a recurring annual disaster in the region.
The former finance minister also called on Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan to formally convey the proposal to Indonesia, arguing that a standing regional firefighting force with rapid deployment powers would enable ASEAN to respond more effectively to forest fires and trans-boundary haze incidents.
He added that concerns over national sovereignty should not stand in the way of practical solutions to address a problem that continues to affect millions of people across the region.

Title: Poor students increasingly lured into mule account schemes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 —  Online scam syndicates are increasingly exploiting financially vulnerable university and college students by recruiting them as mule account holders, sometimes offering payments of as little as RM40.
Kosmo
reported Malaysian International Humanitarian Organisation (MHO) secretary-general Datuk Hishamuddin Hashim saying the trend has become more prevalent in several states, particularly among students in the Klang Valley, Selangor and Penang.
He said syndicates specifically target students from low-income families who are struggling to meet their daily expenses, using various pretexts to gain access to their banking information.
Among the latest tactics is the use of digital bank accounts, which can be opened online with minimal verification requirements such as a selfie and a copy of an identity card.
The ease of registration has enabled scammers to adapt their methods, moving away from the traditional practice of renting or buying physical ATM cards.
“These are modern-day mule account tactics. The modus operandi has evolved significantly,” Hishamuddin said.
He said students are commonly approached through advertisements for part-time jobs, paid surveys or education loan schemes.
In one frequently reported scam, students are instructed to open a bank account as part of a supposed recruitment process. Once the account is created, they are informed that they were unsuccessful in securing the job, unaware that the account may later be used for illegal transactions.
Other victims are tricked into providing personal details under the guise of participating in surveys, only to discover later that the information had been used to facilitate banking activities without their knowledge.
Hishamuddin said students seeking financial aid were also vulnerable. Some are persuaded to disclose online banking usernames and passwords after being told the details are needed for loan disbursements.
“The victims are often in urgent need of money and do not question the requests,” he said.
Many only realise they have become linked to criminal activities when contacted by police investigators or when their bank accounts are frozen following fraud complaints.
Beyond the immediate financial consequences, victims may face multiple investigations and long-term repercussions, including potential criminal records.
The issue has surfaced in several court cases involving students. Among them was a law student who was fined after admitting to allowing his bank account to be used for unlawful transactions, while another college student was charged with acting as a mule account holder for an online scam syndicate.
The growing problem had earlier prompted Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to warn that increasing numbers of students were being recruited by scam networks, with some allegedly offered monthly payments of between RM1,000 and RM2,000 in return for the use of their bank accounts.

Title: Former Negeri Sembilan MB asks for space, says no media statement for now
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — Journalists have gathered at several locations, including the Menteri Besar’s office here, as they await further developments in the political crisis in Negeri Sembilan.
This follows Datuk Ismail Lasim’s resignation as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar yesterday.
However, Ismail said in a brief message that he would not be meeting the media for the time being.
“I apologise, but I am unable to meet reporters for now. I will not be holding a press conference or issuing any media statement. Thank you,” he told Bernama in a WhatsApp message today.
He also asked for space and time following his resignation.
Yesterday, Barisan Nasional (BN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said BN chairman and UMNO president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy of Ismail’s resignation letter submitted to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Ismail, 67, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, was sworn in as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar on Aug 2.
In the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, BN won 18 seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven, allowing the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. — Bernama

Title: ‘Show me one plot in KL with no value’: Dr Akmal Saleh challenges Hannah Yeoh over RM4.67m land premium
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh has challenged Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh to identify any parcel of land in Kuala Lumpur that has no value, amid questions over the reduction of a land premium from RM4.67 million to RM1,000.
In a Facebook post, Akmal argued that the land belonging to the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) retained its value despite claims that it had no commercial potential.
He pointed out that the agency responsible had assessed the premium for the 99-year lease at RM4.67 million, questioning the basis for reducing it to a nominal RM1,000.
“When the government sets a nominal premium of RM1,000, what changes is the amount payable. The original valuation remains RM4.67 million.
“So, YB Minister, on what basis was the RM4.67 million premium reduced to RM1,000?” he asked.
Akmal also challenged Hannah to identify even a single plot of land in Kuala Lumpur that genuinely had no value.
“And if there really is land in Kuala Lumpur that has absolutely no value, try showing me just one lot. I would also like to know where it is,” he said.
His remarks follow Hannah’s explanation that the KLSCAH site no longer had commercial value as it could not be developed into condominiums or shopping malls, but could only be used for institutional and heritage purposes.
According to a report by
Berita Harian
, the government approved a 99-year lease renewal for the property on November 14, with the land premium set at RM1,000 instead of the earlier estimated RM4.67 million.
The Federal Territories Land Committee had approved the surrender and re-alienation of the land for institutional use on September 14.
An approval letter dated October 1 set the premium at RM1,000, while the total amount payable under the official land notice was RM5,011, including the first year’s land rent and administrative charges.
The annual land rent was fixed at RM3,151.
The decision followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s commitment to consider special arrangements to preserve the historic building after visiting it during Chinese New Year celebrations on February 17.

Title: Government cannot terminate Pan Borneo contracts at will, warns Nanta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 —  The government could face legal action and damage claims if it arbitrarily terminates contracts awarded to contractors for the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway (LPB) project without following established procedures and legal requirements.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said contract termination was not a decision that could be taken lightly, as contractors had legal rights, including the right to apply for an Extension of Time (EOT) if project delays were caused by factors beyond their control.
These include delays in site handovers arising from the government’s failure to finalise compensation payments for land acquisition.
“If the (state) Department of Lands and Surveys has not settled land acquisition compensation, contractors cannot access the site because landowners will not allow them to do so. In such cases, they are indeed entitled to claim an extension of time.
“We cannot simply terminate contracts at will. If we fail to comply with proper governance or legal requirements, they could take us to court and claim damages, which the government would then have to pay,” he said.
He was speaking as a guest on Bernama TV’s
Ruang Bicara
programme, titled “Empowering National Infrastructure Towards Sustainable Development”, last night.
Elaborating on land acquisition for the highway project, Nanta acknowledged that the process had also been delayed by political interference at the local level.
“We must admit that when directives (for land acquisition) are issued, political interference sometimes occurs. Local political leaders may intervene by making appeals, resulting in delays and prolonged waiting periods.
“This does not even take into account the costs and complexities involved in relocating utility infrastructure, such as cables and water pipes,” he said.
On the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway Phase 1 project, which the 2020 Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) highlighted for its slow progress, Nanta explained that the figure reflected the combined performance of all 35 work packages under Phases 1A and 1B.
He said Phase 1B, comprising 19 work packages, only commenced in September 2024 but had already achieved 26 per cent physical progress and 23 per cent financial progress.
“As for Phase 1A, comprising 15 packages, which began much earlier, I acknowledge that there were serious shortcomings. However, physical progress has now reached 90 per cent, with four packages fully completed.
“The packages experiencing significant delays are Packages 1 and 2, located near the Sarawak border.
“If all 35 packages are combined into a single dataset, the overall progress percentage is inevitably pulled down by the problematic packages under Phase 1A,” he said.
Nanta said the Works Ministry (KKR) had accepted the findings and observations in the Auditor-General’s Report without taking a defensive stance. The ministry had also reorganised the deployment of Public Works Department (JKR) Sabah personnel to improve project administration and implementation on the ground.
He said the ministry was targeting completion of the entire Pan Borneo Highway project by 2030, guided by four key measures: a Completion Recovery Plan, ensuring land readiness, implementing cost controls for Phase 1B, and using an Audit Compliance Tracker to ensure all 13 findings in the Auditor-General’s Report were addressed within the stipulated timeframes.
The ministry had also established a Steering Committee, co-chaired by the State Secretary, to expedite coordination among agencies responsible for land acquisition and utility matters in Sabah.
In another development, Nanta said the Sarawak-Sabah Link Road (SSLR) project would feature the construction of Borneo’s first tunnel, which is expected to be more than two kilometres long.
He said the route would connect northern Sarawak to Sabah via Lawas, bypassing Brunei and eliminating the need for travellers to pay transit fees or undergo passport and immigration checks.
He added that the SSLR was being built to R3-standard rural road specifications, which are lower than the R5 standard used for the Pan Borneo Highway, but would nevertheless play an important role in improving connectivity to the interior areas of both states. — Bernama

Title: Thai drug haul: Two of five arrested Malaysians linked to previous narcotics offences
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 —  Two of the five Malaysian men arrested by Thai authorities on suspicion of smuggling 240 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine last Wednesday were found to have previous drug-related criminal records.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, aged 37 and 39, from Kedah, had three and one previous narcotics-related offences respectively.
“The three other men, aged 34, 38 and 40, had no drug-related criminal records,” he said when contacted.
Hussein said checks revealed that all five men had entered Thailand through the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex in Kedah between Oct 24 and Nov 9.
He said the department had received information on the arrests from Thailand’s Narcotics Suppression Bureau (NSB), which conducted an operation with the Royal Thai Police (RTP) Metropolitan Police Division 7, in cooperation with the military and the Office of the Narcotics Control Board (ONCB), at four locations.
He said the operation was launched following intelligence on a methamphetamine smuggling syndicate operating across the Malaysia-Thailand border.
“The first raid in Prachuap Khiri Khan province led to the arrest of two Malaysian men and the seizure of 120 kg of methamphetamine from a black Toyota Alphard multi-purpose vehicle (MPV).
“The second raid resulted in the seizure of another 120 kg of methamphetamine concealed in another black Toyota Alphard,” he said, adding that two local Thai women, aged 24 and 25, were also arrested in the operation.
Hussein said Bukit Aman NCID, through the Kedah and Perlis contingents, was working with Thai authorities to expand investigations into the case.
“We are seeking cooperation from the NSB and RTP to obtain further information on the individuals arrested and identify the networks of the syndicate suspected to be involved in Malaysia,” he said.
Earlier, media reports said five Malaysians and two Thai women had been arrested by Thai police in a special operation against a drug syndicate in Prachuap Khiri Khan and Bangkok.
Investigations by Thai authorities found that the syndicate was run by masterminds in Malaysia, with suspects promised between 500,000 and one million baht (approximately RM61,000 to RM122,000) for each successful delivery. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia proposes new funding sources for Asean haze mitigation efforts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysia has proposed that the potential involvement of the agriculture, insurance sectors and health-related entities be explored to strengthen funding efforts to address transboundary haze pollution at the Asean level.
The Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry said the proposal is in line with Article 20 of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP).
“Potential funding sources include international organisations, regional financial institutions, donor agencies and other agreed stakeholders,” the ministry said in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat to Datuk Seri Tuan Ibharim Tuan Man (PN-Kubang Kerian) yesterday.
According to the ministry, Malaysia’s proposal has received the support of member countries of the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee, and it was agreed that the Asean Secretariat explore and assess the proposal’s feasibility.
“Discussions and negotiations on this proposal will continue at the 21st Meeting of the Committee and Conference of the Parties to the AATHP in December 2026 in Vietnam,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Sri Muda floodgate expected to resume automatic operations within six weeks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The electricity supply issue that has resulted in the Sri Muda floodgate in Shah Alam, Selangor, being operated manually is expected to be resolved within six weeks, said Kota Raja Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said the assurance was given by the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) when he visited the floodgate today to assess the monsoon season preparedness.
Mohamad, who is also Agriculture and Food Security Minister, said resolving the issue was important to enable the floodgate to resume automatic operations.
“I hope this commitment can be fulfilled within the promised timeframe for the safety and peace of mind of residents.
“While awaiting the full restoration of the automatic system, I hope the DID will ensure that operations, water-level monitoring and staff preparedness remain at the highest level, especially during heavy rain,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
He said the department had also informed him that the water level of Sungai Klang in Taman Sri Muda remained stable, but continuous monitoring was crucial, particularly following the flash floods that hit the area on Nov 8.
Mohamad said flood management went beyond monitoring water levels and ensuring floodgates functioned efficiently, as it also involved safeguarding the lives, homes and livelihoods of thousands of residents.
“We do not want past tragedies to recur simply because of weaknesses in infrastructure preparedness and maintenance,” he said.
He said the devastating floods in December 2021 remained etched in the memories of Taman Sri Muda residents, as many homes were submerged, properties destroyed, and some families suffered the loss of loved ones.
He also urged residents of Taman Sri Muda and surrounding areas to remain vigilant and heed announcements from the authorities. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia retains seat on ITU Council for second consecutive term
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — Malaysia has retained its seat on the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council for a second consecutive term, covering 2027 to 2030, following its re-election at the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) in Doha, Qatar.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in a statement today, said the re-election reflected the continued confidence of ITU member states in Malaysia’s contributions and role in advancing digital development internationally.
“As one of the 48 countries elected to the ITU Council, Malaysia will continue to play a role in shaping the strategic direction and key decisions of the United Nations (UN) specialised agency responsible for telecommunications and digital technologies.
“The Communications Ministry and MCMC would like to express their deepest appreciation to ITU member states for their trust and support,” the statement said.
It added that Malaysia’s re-election not only recognised the country’s contributions but also provided an opportunity for it to continue helping shape a more connected, inclusive and secure digital future for all.
MCMC said during its 2023-2026 term, Malaysia contributed to efforts to bridge the digital divide through the ITU’s Partner2Connect Digital Coalition, including by supporting underserved communities and developing countries through scholarships, specialised training and knowledge-sharing initiatives
At the regional level, Malaysia, through the Asia-Pacific Telecommunity (APT), also strengthened cooperation and advanced common policy positions on spectrum management, technical standards and improving the effectiveness of ITU institutions.
Malaysia’s contributions also received international recognition, with the country winning World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS) Prizes for two consecutive years: the Nadi Digital Inclusive Project in 2025 and the ASEAN 5G Skills Framework and Capacity Development Platform in 2026.
MCMC was also named a WSIS Platinum Partner in both years.
The statement added that the National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) were recognised as part of the ITU’s Digital Transformation Centres (DTC) network in April 2026, acknowledging Malaysia’s community-based approach to expanding access to digital skills training, particularly among underserved communities.
“Guided by the vision of ‘Inclusivity for an Equitable Future’, Malaysia will continue to promote a connected, inclusive and secure digital society through national initiatives such as the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), Nadi and the Safer Internet Campaign (KIS),” the statement said.
For the 2027-2030 term, MCMC said Malaysia would adopt a more comprehensive approach to bridging the digital divide by going beyond internet connectivity to expand access and strengthen digital skills, ensuring that developing countries could also benefit from emerging technologies.
“Malaysia will also champion online safety, digital trust and cybersecurity resilience. This includes leveraging emerging technologies and quantum-resistant security solutions to strengthen protection against cyber threats and safeguard critical digital infrastructure,” the statement added. — Bernama

Title: No new deadline set for South China Sea code negotiations, says Anwar
Article:
MANILA, Nov 17 — Asean and China have not set a new deadline for concluding negotiations on the South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC), although both sides have reaffirmed their commitment to expediting the process, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said Asean leaders and Chinese Premier Li Qiang acknowledged the progress made in the negotiations during the Asean-China Summit here yesterday.
Asked whether the talks could extend beyond the original end-2026 target, Anwar said he believed they could, given the progress achieved so far.
“When there is clearly progress in these negotiations, we should not give a deadline that may frustrate the progress. If there is just a negotiation without any progress, then I can understand. But in this case, there has been,” he told Malaysian media after attending the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits here.
Anwar said China had reaffirmed its commitment to pressing ahead with the negotiations and concluding them swiftly.
He said China has also agreed in principle to the broad parameters of the code, including provisions aimed at safeguarding peace and ensuring passage through the South China Sea, although details remained to be worked out.
Meanwhile, Anwar described the negotiations as being at a “critical juncture”, warning that prolonged delays could create opportunities for external powers to intervene in the region.
He said the initial target was to conclude the negotiations by the end of this year and stressed the importance of maintaining momentum despite the progress achieved.
“I just want to urge them not to delay the process. I do not want other powers to intervene and exploit this vacuum to assert their role in the region,” he said.
International media reported that the South China Sea is subject to overlapping maritime claims, with China’s extensive claims overlapping the exclusive economic zones (EEZs) of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam.
A functional COC is seen as important in preventing an escalation of tensions and establishing mechanisms to manage incidents at sea. — Bernama

Title: Anwar praises Philippines’ stewardship of Asean summit
Article:
MANILA, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has praised the Philippines’ Asean chairmanship this year, particularly for ensuring substantive discussions on various issues of regional importance.
He said the Philippines had done its best in carrying out its responsibilities in hosting the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, which brought together leaders of member states and the bloc’s dialogue partners.
“I think the Philippines has done its best, and all the discussions that took place were substantive,” he told Malaysian media here yesterday when asked about his experience attending the summit.
Anwar leads the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits from Nov 15 to 17 under the Philippines’ chairmanship, themed “Navigating Our Future, Together”.
Commenting on Malaysia’s achievements during its Asean chairmanship last year, Anwar expressed pride in the successful organisation of the meetings and the commitment of officials at all levels in ensuring their smooth conduct.
“I am proud of Malaysia’s organisation… it is not me saying so, but other countries continue to express their admiration,” he said.
The Prime Minister said the positive feedback received covered not only the organisation of the meetings but also the substance and quality of discussions held throughout Malaysia’s chairmanship.
He said a more significant development was the growing commitment among Asean member states to further strengthen regional cooperation despite differences in views.
“We are also proud to see progress and increased commitment among Asean countries to foster a spirit of cooperation despite differences of opinion among countries,” he said.
Anwar also touched on Timor-Leste’s Asean membership during Malaysia’s chairmanship last year, describing it as one of the significant achievements in the development of the regional bloc.
He said Asean’s agreement to allow Dili to assume the chairmanship in 2029 would require continued cooperation and assistance from all member states.
In this regard, he said Malaysia, together with several other member states, including Indonesia and Singapore, had provided assistance to strengthen Timor-Leste’s capacity to participate in Asean. — Bernama

Title: Appeals Court upholds dismissal of medical negligence suit against Penang General Hospital
Article:
PUTRJAJAYA, Nov 17 — The Court of Appeal today dismissed an appeal by a religious teacher in a medical negligence suit against the Malaysian government, medical personnel and staff of the Penang General Hospital, where he was treated after a road accident.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin and Datuk Amarjeet Singh today unanimously dismissed and ordered Mohammad Nabill Sajid Mohammad Aslam Sajid to pay RM30,000 as cost.
In delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Shahnaz said the court found no applicable error by the High Court judge which is primarily involved in findings of fact based on evidence adduced.
She said in medical damages cases, the applicable standard is that of a reasonable and competent medical practitioner.
“Differences in medical opinion do not amount to medical negligence if treatment is supported by a reasonable body of medical opinion. What this entails is that a doctor is not negligent merely because another doctor would have acted differently,” she said.
Mohammad Nabill was involved in a road accident on July 11, 2020 and sustained severe injuries to his spinal cord. He was 21 years old then.
He sued the government and 31 medical personnel and staff of the Penang General Hospital claiming that they failed to act in accordance with their professional duty and standard of care to be observed during his treatment, causing him to sustain serious disabilities.
He said as a result of the serious disabilities, he would have to depend on others for all activities of his daily living for the rest of his life claiming that the defendants failed to carry out a decompression surgery to relieve the pressure on his spinal cord to salvage the spinal cord.
He was claiming for RM400,000 in general damages for pain and suffering and loss of amenities, RM2,943,078 for nursing care, RM212,726 for loss of income, RM701,600 for cost of disable-friendly motor vehicle, RM58,912 for cost of modification to his house, RM29,005 in special damages and RM500,000 in aggravated damages.
The defendants claimed that they had exercised proper professional care and adhered to standard clinical operating procedures at all times. They claimed at that time Mohammad Nabill was not stable enough to undergo the decompression surgery.
The High Court had dismissed Mohammad Nabill’s suit in April 2025 after finding that there was no breach of duty of care.
At the Court of Appeal today, lawyers Datuk M. Karuppanan and M. Diveena appeared for Mohammad Nabill while senior federal counsel Mohd ‘Afif Ali and Federal Counsel Amirul Hisyam Azedi Noor appeared for the government and the medical personnel and staff. — Bernama

Title: Man jailed, caned for posing as Selangor Crown Prince's aide in celebrity scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A man who impersonated the aide-de-camp (ADC) to the Raja Muda of Selangor to cheat a celebrity in a property purchase scam was sentenced to one year’s imprisonment and two strokes of the cane by the Magistrate’s Court here yesterday.
Magistrate Amirul Asyraf Abdul Rasid handed down the sentence on Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, after he pleaded guilty to the charge. The court ordered that the jail term take effect from his arrest on Oct 27.
His fiancée, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, who was charged with the same offence, pleaded not guilty.
According to the charge, the couple, both unemployed, had cheated a 35-year-old male celebrity through an offer to purchase a property, inducing him to transfer RM30,000 in two transactions into Al Zulfadly’s bank account at Jalan Wangsa Delima 11, Wangsa Maju on May 10 and 12, 2024.
The charge was framed under Section 420 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, which provides for imprisonment of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurul Farhanah Arul Hisham sought an appropriate sentence for Al Zulfadly, while Nurul Nur Syahirah was initially offered bail of RM5,000 with one surety.
However, National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK) lawyer Mohd Ridzwan Warisi, representing Al Zulfadly, sought a minimum jail term, to take effect from the date of his arrest, citing his responsibility to support his mother and the fact that his guilty plea had saved the court’s time.
Lawyer Shah Rizal Abdul Manan, representing Nurul Nur Syahirah, also sought a lower bail amount, saying that she was unemployed and financially supported by her parents.
The court subsequently allowed her bail at RM3,000 with one surety and fixed Dec 16 for mention for the submission of documents.
Earlier, Al Zulfadly also pleaded guilty to four counts of cheating at the Sessions Court here, while Nurul Nur Syahirah pleaded not guilty to similar charges.
Judge Norma Ismail fixed tomorrow for the submission of case facts and sentencing for Al Zulfadly, while allowing Nurul Nur Syahirah bail of RM15,000, with additional conditions that she report to a nearby police station monthly and surrender her passport to the court.
The couple were accused of cheating a female doctor through offers involving a property at Eco Ardence and a luxury vehicle, a Lexus LM 500h, inducing her to transfer RM155,000 through four online transactions into Al Zulfadly’s bank account at Jalan Ampang between July 2 and 19.
The charge was brought under Section 420 of the Penal Code. The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Batrisyia Mohd Khusri.
On November 12, the couple were charged at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court with cheating involving the sale of an auction vehicle worth RM30,000. The following day, they were charged at the Klang Magistrate’s Court over another alleged scam involving the sale of an auction vehicle worth RM40,000.
The Klang case was transferred to the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court and is scheduled for mention on Nov 20 for the submission of case facts and sentencing for Al Zulfadly, who pleaded guilty, while Nurul Nur Syahirah pleaded not guilty. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: China to boost AI technology transfer, training for Asean
Article:
MANILA, Nov 17 — China has agreed to strengthen cooperation with Malaysia and other Asean member states in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing aspects of technology transfer and additional training, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said that AI and cybersecurity were also major focuses during discussions with dialogue partners at the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits here.
“In all discussions regarding AI and cybersecurity, including with Australia and South Korea, we emphasised the importance of stepping up efforts in both fields,” he told the Malaysian media after attending the conference sessions here yesterday.
Anwar is leading the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits taking place from Nov 15 to 17 under the chairmanship of the Philippines, themed “Navigating Our Future, Together”.
Malaysia is currently acting as the country coordinator for Asean-China dialogue relations.
Anwar added that Asean also placed special emphasis on micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in discussions with China, South Korea, and Australia touching on the energy and trade sectors.
“MSMEs are our economic strength in Asean. If we focus solely on large-scale investments, this group will be left behind,” he said.
Meanwhile, commenting on the Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) signed on Saturday, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the pact marked an important first step towards making cross-border payments easier and harmonising customs declarations across member states.
“Both measures could boost intra-Asean trade, with harmonised customs declarations allowing member states to cross-check trade information,” Johari said.
He added that Asean was aiming to work towards a common digital platform for its member states over the next 180 days or so.
Asked whether the target could be met, he said it depended on how quickly Asean member states moved.
“If they want to move quickly, they will. If they take their time, it will take longer,” he said. — Bernama

Title: No reshuffle: Government stable, Cabinet working well, says Anwar
Article:
MANILA, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reaffirmed that the government remains stable and is fully focused on implementing policies and fulfilling its responsibilities to the people rather than entertaining speculation about a Cabinet reshuffle.
He said there was no pressing need to reshuffle the Cabinet at present, despite various views emerging following DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke’s resignation as Transport Minister.
“The government is stable now, policies are discussed comprehensively in the Cabinet, and I work with ministers from various parties.
“We work, share, discuss and have a common position, including on sensitive bilateral, multilateral and Asean issues,” he told a media conference on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits here yesterday.
Anwar is leading the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits from November 15 to 17 under the Philippines’ chairmanship, themed “Navigating Our Future, Together”.
On Loke’s resignation, Anwar said he respected the DAP leader’s principled stance, although he had earlier asked him to reconsider his decision.
“He (Loke), on principle, asked me to accept his resignation, which I have yet to do. But I respect his position because it is important to him to uphold the principles he stands for.
“In coalition governments in several countries, this is not unusual. When there is a coalition, sometimes the situation at the federal level differs from that at the state level,” he said.
On November 10, Loke announced his resignation from the Cabinet with immediate effect following the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision allowing former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest from that day.
Elaborating, the Prime Minister said political discussions remained open, including through formal and informal meetings with party leaders and members of the administration to address any differences of opinion.
At the same time, Anwar dismissed claims seeking to exaggerate alleged instability within the government, describing them as merely a political campaign agenda by certain quarters.
“What is being exaggerated is purely a campaign agenda. But for now, stay the course, continue to work. What’s important, we deliver what is best for this country,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim resigns
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — Datuk Ismail Lasim has resigned as the Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan, said Barisan Nasional (BN) Secretary-General Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir.
Zambry said that BN Chairman and UMNO President Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi received a copy of the resignation letter, which was addressed and sent to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, yesterday.
Accordingly, he said Ahmad Zahid will submit proposed candidates for the new Menteri Besar to be presented before Tuanku Muhriz in line with the provisions of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution (UUTKNS).
“BN respects the decision and extends its gratitude for Datuk Ismail Lasim’s service and contributions throughout his tenure as the Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
“BN hopes this decision can open a new chapter to restore political stability and ensure the administration of Negeri Sembilan resumes functioning smoothly,” he said in a statement on BN’s official Facebook page tonight.
Zambry added that BN will give its full cooperation to ensure the leadership transition process proceeds in an orderly manner, taking into account the majority standing of State Legislative Assembly members (ADUN) as well as the royal assent of Tuanku Muhriz.
In the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election (PRN) on Aug 2, BN won 18 state seats while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven seats, enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. — Bernama

Title: Quartz ridges, ivory tusks and ‘perahu payang’: How four flagship ECRL stations celebrate local heritage and geography
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — As trial operations accelerate ahead of commercial passenger services next month, four flagship terminals along the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) are turning routine train stops into striking architectural tributes to regional culture and local geography.
Master planner Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) is conducting final trial runs across the rail corridor ahead of the planned commercial rollout on December 12.
Rather than relying on generic, utilitarian station boxes, the four major hubs of Terminal Bersepadu Gombak (ITT Gombak), KotaSAS in Pahang, Kuala Terengganu, and Kota Bharu in Kelantan showcase distinctive architectural language that celebrate the craftsmanship, folklore, and natural landmarks of their respective states.
The ITT Gombak ECRL Station draws inspiration from the Gombak Selangor Quartz Ridge, a geological landmark. — Picture courtesy of Malaysia Rail Link
At the western gateway, ITT Gombak takes its design cues from the nearby Gombak Selangor Quartz Ridge, previously known as the Klang Gates Quartz Ridge.
Stretching over 14 kilometres in length and 200 metres in width, the world’s longest quartz dyke serves as both a panoramic backdrop visible from arriving trains and the conceptual foundation for the station’s crystalline silhouette.
Mirroring the sharp geometry of cleaved quartz crystal, the terminal features a dynamic, weather-responsive reflective glass façade that shifts tones under changing light conditions.
The KotaSAS ECRL Station draws inspiration from Pahang's longstanding relationship with elephants. — Picture courtesy of Malaysia Rail Link
Crossing the Titiwangsa Range into Pahang, the KotaSAS station in Kuantan draws inspiration from the crossed elephant tusks that anchor the state’s official coat of arms, a motif prominently cast into its sweeping roofline.
The design honours Pahang’s historical wild herds of Asian elephants, evoking their traditional significance in royal processions, ancient statecraft, and battle as enduring symbols of martial valour.
Complementing the sculptural roof, the entire exterior is coated in pristine white, mirroring the natural ivory tones of the heraldic emblem.
The Kuala Terengganu ECRL Station draws inspiration from the state's rich maritime heritage, particularly its traditional boat-building craftsmanship. — Picture Courtesy of Malaysia Rail Link
Further north along the eastern coast, the Kuala Terengganu station celebrates the state’s maritime lineage and world-renowned boat-building heritage through undulating roof profiles that evoke rolling ocean swells and wooden hulls.
The main façade draws direct inspiration from the
perahu payang
, the majestic traditional wooden vessel named after the
pukat payang
fishing net that long sustained coastal fishing communities.
By translating these seafaring contours into structural steel, the station pays homage to centuries of coastal seafaring culture.
The Kota Bharu ECRL Station draws inspiration from the state's rich architectural heritage, incorporating traditional Kelantanese design elements into its modern structure. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
At the northern terminus in Kelantan, the Kota Bharu station presents a contemporary interpretation of classical Malay palace architecture, incorporating elements reminiscent of Istana Jahar and the Islamic Museum.The exterior face prominently adapts the intricate
janda berhias
motif, an elaborate geometric wood-carving pattern that literally translates to “adorned widow”, historically reserved for royal residences and aristocratic manors.
The terminal’s grand entrance archway incorporates the
pemeleh
, the carved decorative timber panels traditionally fixed to the gables of classical Kelantanese timber houses.
Crowned above, the roof incorporates the
ekor itik
, or ducktail, an upward-curving ornamental feature historically linked to royalty and nobility. Inside the main concourse, the botanical
ketam guri
motif is rendered across perforated acoustic panels, floor tiling, and ceilings, scaling the delicate visual geometry of Kelantanese
batik
into a grand modern transport hub.
The ketam guri motif seen here at the waiting hall is closely associated with the traditional arts and cultural heritage of Peninsular Malaysia's east coast. — Picture by Firdaus Latif

Title: Selangor identifies 56 flood hotspots ahead of Northeast Monsoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Rainfall exceeding 100 millimetres within just over two hours could trigger flash floods in Kampung Melayu Subang and surrounding areas if rivers and local drainage systems are unable to cope with the volume of water.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the two main rivers contributing to overflow in the area were Sungai Damansara and Sungai Buluh.
“In areas currently at risk of flooding, the overflowing water comes from Sungai Damansara and Sungai Buluh. In Kampung Melayu Subang, flooding is also influenced by overflow from the local drainage system,” he told Bernama today.
He said the overflow could also affect several other areas, including Shah Alam, Puncak Alam, Paya Jaras and Kampung Kubu Gajah, before flowing towards Kampung Parit Mahang, Ijok, Cerakah and Kampung Bukit Kuching, eventually reaching Kuala Selangor.
In preparation for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), Selangor JBPM has identified 56 flood hotspots and 232 flood-prone areas statewide.
Klang has the highest number of flood hotspots, with 13, followed by Petaling (11), Gombak (10), Hulu Langat (nine), Kuala Selangor (six), Sepang (three), and Kuala Langat and Hulu Selangor with two each. No flood hotspots have been recorded in Sabak Bernam.
Hulu Langat has the highest number of flood-prone areas at 37, followed by Klang (33), Sepang (32), Kuala Selangor and Gombak (29 each), Petaling (27), Kuala Langat (22), Hulu Selangor (12) and Sabak Bernam (11).
Ashrul Riezal said the department had 1,603 firefighters and 1,251 volunteer members  on standby, supported by 71 rescue boats, 12 operational lorries and 68 four-wheel-drive vehicles to deal with possible flooding during the monsoon.
Kampung Melayu Subang is among the areas in Selangor prone to recurring floods. Heavy rain earlier this month caused several homes there to be inundated.
Following the incident, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Nov 3 directed that the implementation of the nearly RM700 million Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara Flood Mitigation Projects be expedited. — Bernama

Title: Pasir Gudang MP hands over phone as police probe viral poem
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Pasir Gudang Member of Parliament Hassan Abdul Karim gave his statement at Bukit Aman today regarding his poem titled
Patik Tak Rela
which went viral on social media.
He arrived at the police headquarters at 2:50 pm to give his statement to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT), with the recording of his statement conducted by the investigating officer starting at 3:00 pm.
“I gave my full cooperation and answered nearly 20 questions posed throughout the investigation session,” he said when met by reporters after finishing his statement.
He informed that his mobile phone was also handed over to the police to assist with further investigations.
However, Hassan declined to comment on the meaning of the poem, expressing concern that his remarks might contradict the official statement already recorded.
“The poem has already gone viral, so it is up to the public to make their own interpretations. I cannot explain it here,” he said.
It is understood that the investigation is being conducted under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. — Bernama

Title: Two held as KPDN confiscates 27,000 hair dye products bearing suspected unauthorised halal logo
Article:
TASEK GELUGOR, Nov 16 — The Penang branch of the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye products worth RM1.08 million suspected of misusing the Malaysian halal logo without a valid Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM) in a raid on a warehouse in Kampung Selamat here today.
Penang KPDN director S. Jegan said the seizure was made during an inspection conducted at about 1pm following complaints and three weeks of intelligence gathering by the ministry's enforcement officers.
"In the raid, we seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye products stored in the warehouse and detained two company employees, a local woman and a Chinese national man, both in their 30s, to assist in investigations.
"Preliminary investigations found that the products were suspected of displaying the Malaysian halal logo although the company failed to produce valid halal certification documents to substantiate the use of the logo,” he told a media conference at the warehouse here today.
He said investigations also revealed that the hair dye products were imported from China and stored at a warehouse rented by the company before being marketed online through social media and e-commerce platforms such as TikTok, Shopee and Lazada.
Jegan said the company was believed to have been operating for the past six months, with an estimated 600,000 units of the products sold during that period, each bottle of hair dye retailing at RM40.
He said the company's modus operandi included displaying suspected fake halal certificates in advertisements on social media and e-commerce platforms, as well as engaging popular social media influencers and affiliate agents to convince consumers of the products' halal status.
"Our inspection also found that the halal certificate displayed in their promotional materials actually belonged to another company and not the company marketing the products. The Malaysian halal logo was also displayed on the product packaging despite the company not having a valid SPHM for the products,” he said.
He said the matter was particularly concerning as the hair dye was a personal care product used by various segments of society, including senior citizens, and misuse of the halal logo could mislead consumers and undermine confidence in the integrity of the country's halal certification system.
He said further investigations were underway, including efforts to trace the company owner, and the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 (Act 730).
He advised consumers to verify the halal status of products through the official website of the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM), particularly before making purchases, and not to rely entirely on sellers' claims or affiliate promotions. — Bernama

Title: Dentist fined RM70,000 over use of unregistered staff for dental work
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 16 — A dentist was fined RM70,000 by the Sessions Court here today after being found guilty of two charges of employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner and allowing the person to perform dental procedures at her clinic two years ago.
Judge Noor Ruzilawati Mohd Noor imposed a fine of RM30,000 for the first charge and RM40,000 for the second, with six and seven months’ imprisonment respectively in default of payment.
Dr Tong Soo Huan, 38, was charged with employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner under the Dental Act 2018 at a dental clinic in Jalan SS21/1 here at 12.50 pm on May 6, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 68 of the Dental Act 2018, which provides for a maximum fine of RM300,000 or imprisonment for up to six years, or both.
She was also charged with allowing an individual who was not registered under the Act to practise dentistry at her clinic on the same date and time, under Section 69(a) of the same Act, which carries the same maximum penalty.
According to the facts of the case, on May 6, 2024, a team of enforcement officers from the Selangor State Health Department conducted an inspection at Dr Tong’s clinic and found a female staff member scanning a patient’s teeth using an iTero Element intraoral scanner.
The inspection found that the staff member was not registered with the Malaysian Dental Council (MDC) as a dental practitioner, while Dr Tong, who was a registered dental practitioner, failed to produce the staff member’s annual practising certificate when requested by the enforcement officers.
Earlier, Health Ministry (MOH) prosecuting officer Dr Haznita Zainal Abidin urged the court to impose substantial fines for both charges in the interest of public safety and patient protection, noting that the offences were of a strict liability nature and involved the integrity of the dental profession.
“The accused not only failed to ensure that a registered dental practitioner was on duty throughout the clinic’s operating hours, but also deliberately instructed and allowed a clinic staff member whose only qualification was the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) to perform dental procedures, namely intraoral scanning using specialised medical device equipment at the accused’s premises.
“An oral scanning procedure using an intraoral scanner (iTero Element) requires a high level of expertise to operate. Based on testimony from the Medical Device Authority, the device can only be operated by qualified medical or dental practitioners,” she said.
Dr Haznita said the sentence should send a strong message and serve as a stern lesson to the accused and the entire dental practitioner community in Malaysia not to take shortcuts to cut costs or disregard the law by delegating clinical duties to staff without professional qualifications.
However, lawyer Rejinder Singh, representing Dr Tong, appealed for a lighter fine, arguing that his client was a first-time offender and had no previous record of offences under the Dental Act 2018.
“The offence committed was a technical violation and did not involve any criminal element, as a patient had come to the clinic for treatment while Dr Tong was out for lunch at the time.
“The accused is aware of her actions and regrets not exercising greater vigilance in supervising the clinic staff. She has pledged to ensure stricter control measures in the future,” the lawyer said. — Bernama
